description: Die katholische Kirche umfasst die weltweite Gemeinschaft aller Christen, die sich als katholisch verstehen. An der Spitze der Glaubensgemeinschaft steht der Papst im Vatikan, der zugleich Bischof von Rom ist.

title: Kaja Kallas
description: Kaja Kallas ist seit 2024 Außenbeauftragte der Europäischen Union. Sie kommt aus Estland und war dort von 2021 bis 2024 Premierministerin.

title: Marshall-Inseln
description: Die Marshall-Inseln sind ein Staat im Pazifik. Mit nicht viel mehr als 40.000 Einwohnern gehören sie zu den kleinsten Ländern der Welt. Durch den Klimawandel ist die Inselgruppe von Überflutung bedroht.

title: Die Union aus CDU und CSU
description: Als Union bezeichnet man die konservativen deutschen Schwesterparteien Christlich Demokratische Union (CDU) und Christlich-Soziale Union (CSU). Die CSU tritt nur in Bayern, die CDU in allen übrigen Bundesländern an.

title: António Costa
description: Der Portugiese António Costa ist seit dem 1. Dezember 2024 Präsident des Europäischen Rates. Von 2015 bis 2024 war er Premierminister Portugals. Geboren wurde er am 17. Juli 1961 in Lissabon.

title: Giorgia Meloni
description: Die ultrarechte Politikerin aus Rom ist seit Oktober 2022 Ministerpräsidentin Italiens. Unter Silvio Berlusconi war sie bereits Ministerin. Sie ist Vorsitzende der rechtsextremen Partei Fratelli d’Italia.

title: Justin Trudeau
description: Justin Trudeau (Sohn von Ex-Premier Pierre Trudeau) war von November 2015 bis März 2025 Kanadas 23. Premierminister und führte zuletzt eine Minderheitsregierung. Er war von 2013-2025 Vorsitzender der Liberalen Partei.

title: Herbert Kickl
description: Der Politiker Herbert Kickl ist seit Juni 2021 Bundesparteiobmann der rechtspopulistischen und rechtsextremen Freiheitlichen Partei Österreichs (FPÖ). Diese wurde unter ihm 2024 stärkste Kraft im Land.

title: Freiheitliche Partei Österreichs (FPÖ)
description: Die Partei FPÖ gilt als rechtspopulistisch und rechtsextrem. Sie war mehrfach an Bundesregierungen beteiligt. Bei der Nationalratswahl 2024 wurde sie stärkste Kraft, nun wurde sie mit der Regierungsbildung beauftragt.

title: Grönland
description: Grönland ist die größte Insel der Welt und liegt im Arktischen Ozean. Sie gehört zum Königreich Dänemark.

title: Sergej Lawrow
description: Langzeitdiplomat Lawrow sitzt seit 1994 als Vertreter Russlands im UN-Sicherheitsrat. Seit 2004 ist er russischer Außenminister. Seit dem Angriff Moskaus auf die Ukraine 2022 wurde sein Vermögen in der EU eingefroren.

title: DOGE - Trumps umstrittene Behörde für Regierungseffizienz
description: Kahlschlag im US-Beamtenapparat: Zum Amtsantritt rief US-Präsident Trump das Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) unter Führung von Elon Musk ins Leben. Massenentlassungen sorgen für Proteste.

title: Arabische Republik Syrien
description: Mit rund 185.000 km² ist das Land, das an Israel, Jordanien, den Libanon, Irak und die Türkei grenzt, halb so groß wie Deutschland. Kann es sich nach dem Sturz von Assad am 8. Dezember 2024 aus der Dauerkrise befreien?

title: Streit um Migration
description: Migration ist ein politisches Dauerthema. Sie war der entscheidende Faktor im Wahlkampf zur deutschen Bundestagswahl. Und auch auf europäischer Ebene ringen die Staatschefs der EU immer wieder um gemeinsame Lösungen.

title: Regierungswechsel in Deutschland
description: Die neue "schwarz-rote" Koalition aus CDU, CSU und SPD hat ihre Arbeit aufgenommen.

title: Ekrem Imamoglu
description: Ekrem Imamoglu ist ein türkischer Politiker der Republikanischen Volkspartei (CHP) und suspendierter Bürgermeister von Istanbul. Bei den Präsidentschaftswahlen 2028 will er Recep Tayyip Erdogan herausfordern.

title: Rote Armee Fraktion (RAF)
description: Die "Rote Armee Fraktion" (RAF) war eine linksextremistische terroristische Organisation in Deutschland. Bis in die 1990er Jahre verübte sie zahlreiche Anschläge, Banküberfälle und Morde.

title: Die fünf Wirtschaftsweisen
description: Der Sachverständigenrat zur Begutachtung der gesamtwirtschaftlichen Entwicklung wurde 1963 per Gesetz geschaffen und erstellt jedes Jahr ein Gutachten für die Regierung. Die Mitglieder werden Wirtschaftsweise genannt.

title: Organhandel: Illegaler Handel mit Organen und kriminelle Organentnahme
description: Fast überall verboten - aber weltweit gibt es Organhandel als Geschäftsmodell: Lebendspenden gegen Entlohnung oder unter Vorspiegelung falscher Tatsachen, sowie Menschenhandel, Entführung oder Mord zwecks Organentnahme.

title: Kaschmir-Konflikt
description: Ein Anschlag in Kaschmir hat den jahrzehntealten Konflikt zwischen Indien und Pakistan wieder entzündet. Lösungsansätze fehlen.

title: Papst Leo XIV.
description: Seit dem 8. Mai 2025 ist Robert F. Prevost der 267. Papst der katholischen Kirche. Er trägt den Namen Leo XIV., wurde 1955 in den USA geboren, gehört dem Augustinerorden an und wirkte als Missionar und Bischof in Peru.

title: Johann Wadephul
description: Der CDU-Politiker Johann Wadephul ist seit 2009 Bundestagsmitglied und seit Mai 2025 deutscher Außenminister. Der Jurist gilt als enger Vertrauter von Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz.

title: Alexander Dobrindt
description: Der CSU-Politiker Alexander Dobrindt ist seit 2002 Bundestagsmitglied und seit Mai 2025 Bundesinnenminister im Kabinett Merz. Er war im Kabinett Merkel III von 2013 - 2017 Verkehrsminister und zuvor CSU-Generalsekretär.

title: Antigua und Barbuda
description: Der Inselstaat Antigua und Barbuda besteht aus den beiden namensgebenden Hauptinseln sowie 46 kleineren Inseln. Das Archipel liegt zwischen dem Atlantik und der Karibik und ist Mitglied im Commonwealth of Nations.

title: St. Kitts und Nevis
description: Der Inselstaat, auch Föderation St. Kitts und Nevis genannt, gehört zu den Kleinen Antillen in der Karibik. Der Staat besteht aus den beiden namensgebenden Inseln, Hauptstadt ist Basseterre auf St. Kitts.

title: St. Vincent und die Grenadinen
description: Der Archipel St. Vincent und die Grenadinen liegt in der Karibik und besteht aus der namensgebenden Hauptinsel und kleineren Inseln. Die Hauptstadt Kingstown ist das politische und wirtschaftliche Zentrum des Landes.

title: Sicherheits- und Verteidigungspolitik
description: Russlands Angriffskrieg gegen die Ukraine führte zu einer Zeitenwende in Deutschland und Europa. Nach Jahrzehnten des Friedens rückt wieder das Thema Verteidigung in den politischen Fokus - auch durch den Druck der USA.

title: Tag gegen Homo-, Bi-, Inter- und Transfeindlichkeit
description: Der Aktionstag wird seit 2005 jährlich am 17. Mai begangen.

title: Die Entschärfung von Bomben, Minen und Blindgängern
description: Gefährliches Kriegserbe: Auch Jahre und Jahrzehnte nach dem Ende eines Konfliktes liegen noch alte Bomben, Minen und Blindgänger im Boden. Ihre Entschärfung kann lebensgefährlich sein.

title: UEFA Nations League der Männer
description: Die UEFA Nations League gibt es seit 2018. Sie ersetzt für europäische Fußball-Nationalteams Freundschaftsspiele und bietet Zusatzchancen zur Qualifikation für große Turniere. Der Sieger wird in den Finals ermittelt.

title: Fachkräftemangel und Arbeitsmarkt
description: In Deutschland fehlen in vielen Bereichen Fachkräfte - vom Handwerk bis zur IT. Der Mangel bremst die Wirtschaft und stellt Politik und Unternehmen vor große Herausforderungen. Migration könnte das Problem lindern.

title: Big-Tech
description: Big-Tech-Konzerne wie Google, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft und Apple dominieren mit KI, Cloud und Softwarelösungen die digitale Märkte weltweit.

title: Verkehrswende
description: Verkehrswende für den Klimaschutz: Mit E-Mobilität, Ausbau der öffentlichen Verkehrsangebote und weniger Autos sollen CO2-Emissionen sinken und Städte lebenswerter werden.

title: Künstliche Intelligenz und Wirtschaft
description: Künstliche Intelligenz (KI) verändert Prozesse, Berufsbilder und Geschäftsmodelle. Wer profitiert und wer verliert? Ein Blick auf die Chancen und Herausforderungen für Wirtschaft und Arbeitsmarkt.

title: Hitze in Europa
description: Der Klimawandel lässt das Wetter extremer werden - das hat oft negative Folgen für Umwelt, Mensch und Natur.

title: Rüstungsindustrie
description: Rheinmetall und Co freuen sich auf goldene Zeiten: Nicht nur die deutsche Regierung will Milliarden ausgeben, um die Verteidigung zu stärken.

title: Zollstreit
description: US-Präsident Donald Trump bringt Handelspartner der Vereinigten Staaten weltweit unter Druck - die Folgen sind weitreichend.

title: Hunger in der Welt
description: Ein Leben ohne Hunger ist ein Menschenrecht. Dennoch stirbt alle 13 Sekunden ein Kind unter fünf Jahren an den Folgen von Hunger, warnt die Welthungerhilfe. Gleichzeitig kürzen viele Staaten ihre Unterstützung.

title: Robert F. Kennedy Jr.
description: Robert F. Kennedy Jr., auch RFK Jr., ist Gesundheitsminister unter US-Präsident Donald Trump. Kennedy ist als Impfgegner bekannt und vertritt u.a. Die widerlegte These, dass bestimmte Impfungen Autismus verursachen.

title: Karol Nawrocki
description: Karol Tadeusz Nawrocki ist ein polnischer Historiker und Politiker. Er ist seit dem 6. August 2025 Staatspräsident Polens. Zuvor war er von 2021 bis 2025 Leiter des Instituts für Nationales Gedenken.

title: Bayer 04 Leverkusen
description: Der Werksverein steht seit Jahren für attraktiven Fußball und spielt seit seinem Aufstieg 1979 ununterbrochen in der Fußball-Bundesliga. Seinen größten Erfolg feierte Bayer 04 mit dem Double im Jahr 2024.

title: Islam in Europa
description: In Europa leben schätzungsweise 45 Millionen Muslime. Damit ist der Islam nach dem Christentum die zweitgrößte Religion auf dem Kontinent - und zudem die am schnellsten wachsende Religion in Europa.

title: Charlie Kirk
description: Charlie Kirk, umstrittener rechtskonservativer Ideologe, Aktivist und Podcaster, war ein einflussreicher Influencer für junge US-Amerikaner. Der Trump-Unterstützer wurde am 10.09.2025 in Utah erschossen.

title: Huntington-Krankheit
description: Die Huntington-Krankheit ist eine seltene, erblich bedingte Erkrankung des Gehirns. Sie führt zu Bewegungs-, Gedächtnis- und Verhaltensstörungen und endet tödlich. Huntington ist bislang nicht heilbar.

title: El Niño
description: El Niño ist – ebenso wie La Niña - ein Klimaphänomen, das den tropischen Pazifik betrifft und weltweit Temperatur- sowie Niederschlagsmuster verändert.

title: La Niña
description: La Niña ist das Gegenstück zu El Niño. Abgekühlte Meeresoberflächen im tropischen Pazifik führen zu globalen Wetter- und Klimaveränderungen.

title: Tabak / Rauchen
description: Rauchen zählt weltweit zu den führenden Ursachen vermeidbarer Krankheiten. Tabakkonsum schädigt nahezu jedes Organ des menschlichen Körpers.

title: Traditionelle Medizin
description: Traditionelle Medizin umfasst überlieferte Heilmethoden, die in vielen Kulturen bis heute angewendet werden. Ein bekanntes Beispiel ist die traditionelle chinesische Medizin.

title: Traditionelle Chinesische Medizin (TCM)
description: Die Traditionelle Chinesische Medizin ist ein Heilverfahren aus dem Bereich der Alternativmedizin und nutzt Akupunktur, Kräuter und Bewegung zur Wiederherstellung des "inneren Gleichgewichts".

title: Medikamente
description: Medikamente sind chemische oder biologische Wirkstoffe, die Krankheiten vorbeugen, lindern oder heilen sollen.

title: Depression
description: Depression ist eine ernsthafte psychische Erkrankung. Typische Symptome sind anhaltende Niedergeschlagenheit, Hoffnungslosigkeit und der Verlust von Interesse und Freude am Leben.

title: Nobelpreise
description: Die Nobelpreise ehren Leistungen in Physik, Chemie, Medizin, Literatur, Frieden und Wirtschaft. Die Nobelpreise gelten als die weltweit anerkannteste Auszeichnung.

title: Albert Einstein
description: Albert Einstein prägte das Verständnis von Raum, Zeit und Energie. Seine Theorien veränderten Naturwissenschaft und Technik tiefgreifend und machen ihn zu einer Ikone der Wissenschaftsgeschichte.

title: Aufstand der Gen Z
description: In Ländern rund um die Welt gehen junge Menschen auf die Straßen, stürmen Parlamente und bringen Regierungen zu Fall. Der Kampf gegen Korruption und Ungleichheit vereint die Protestbewegung der sogenannten Generation Z.

title: Tierschutz
description: Tierschutz gilt als Spiegel gesellschaftlicher Werte. Zwischen Ethik, Gesetz und Wirtschaft zeigt sich, wie unterschiedlich der Umgang mit Tieren verstanden und umgesetzt wird.

title: Global Fund - Zum Kampf gegen AIDS, Tuberkulose und Malaria
description: Der Fonds mit Sitz in der Schweiz unterstützt seit 2002 weltweit die Bekämpfung der drei großen Infektionskrankheiten AIDS, Tuberkulose und Malaria. Die Finanzierungseinrichtung stellt dafür große Summen bereit.

title: Politik in Deutschland
description: In Deutschland arbeiten Regierung, Parlamente und die sechzehn Bundesländer gemeinsam an politischen Entscheidungen. So wird Demokratie auf mehreren Ebenen umgesetzt.

title: Klimakonferenz COP30
description: Die UN-Klimakonferenz hat in diesem Jahr im brasilianischen Belém getagt. Die Ergebnisse blieben hinter den Erwartungen zurück.

title: Agrarwirtschaft
description: Die Land– und Forstwirtschaft sowie Fischerei tragen in Deutschland weniger als ein Prozent zur Bruttowertschöpfung bei. Sie sind aber wichtige Wirtschaftsbereiche für die Ernährungssicherheit.

title: Islamismus
description: Islamismus ist eine extremistische politische Ideologie, die eine fundamentalistische Form des Islam als Basis für die staatliche Ordnung sieht und die freiheitliche demokratische Grundordnung ablehnt.

title: US-Aktion "Southern Spear"
description: Boote wurden versenkt, Kriegsschiffe entsandt: Offiziell wollen die USA im Karibischen Meer Drogenschmuggel bekämpfen - vor allem aus Venezuela. Doch es könnte noch um andere US-Interessen in der Region gehen.

title: Der Epstein-Skandal
description: Jeffrey Epstein und seine Komplizin Ghislaine Maxwell sollen zahlreiche Mädchen und Frauen missbraucht und Prominenten zugeführt haben. Auch Jahre nach Epsteins Tod in einer Zelle schlägt die Affäre noch hohe Wellen.

title: Nürnberger Prozesse
description: Die Nürnberger Prozesse ab 1945 gelten als Meilenstein des internationalen Rechts. Erstmals mussten sich führende Vertreter eines Staates für Kriegsverbrechen vor einem unabhängigen Tribunal verantworten.

title: Weltraumwirtschaft
description: Europa will im globalen Wachstumsmarkt der Weltraumwirtschaft aufholen. Die wächst jährlich um neun Prozent. Derzeit liegt Europas Anteil bei nur zehn Prozent, doch es wird investiert.

title: Mücken
description: Stechmücken sind fliegende Insekten, die in den meisten Teilen der Welt vorkommen. Ein Bruchteil von den mehr als 3.500 Mückenarten übertragen und verbreiten Krankheiten. Sie sind auch lebenswichtig für die Ökosysteme.

title: US-Sicherheitsstrategie
description: Die neue US-Sicherheitsstrategie mit ihren vehementen Vorwürfen gegen Europa sorgt weiter für Empörung. Was bedeutet die "America First"-Politik des US-Präsidenten Donald Trump?

title: Trumps Militärschlag gegen Venezuela
description: Die USA ‍haben Venezuela angegriffen und den langjährigen Staatschef Nicolás Maduro in ihre Gewalt gebracht. Wie geht es weiter mit dem lateinamerikanischen Land?

title: Javier Milei
description: Ende 2023 wurde der libertäre Rechtspopulist als Präsident Argentiniens vereidigt. Javier Milei nennt sich selbst "Anarcho-Kapitalist". Seine politischen Ziele sind der Rückzug des Staates und das freie Spiel der Kräfte.

title: Reza Pahlavi
description: Nach Jahrzehnten in den USA sorgt er für internationale Aufmerksamkeit: Der Sohn des 1979 gestürzten Schahs ist ins Zentrum der iranischen Protestbewegung gerückt. Was ist die Rolle des Exilpolitikers Reza Pahlavi?

title: US-Einwanderungsbehörde ICE
description: Sie hat weitreichende Befugnisse zur Durchsetzung von Einwanderungs- und Zollgesetzen. Im Auftrag der Trump-Regierung geht sie rigoros gegen Migranten vor.

title: Extremsport
description: Im Extremsport gehen Menschen ans Limit und darüber hinaus: atemberaubende Höhen, riskante Herausforderungen und die Suche nach dem nächsten Adrenalinkick.

title: Brennpunkt Minneapolis
description: Nach einem zweiten Todesfall im Zusammenhang mit Abschiebe-Maßnahmen in Minneapolis verhärten sich die Fronten - nicht nur im Bundesstaat Minnesota, sondern in den USA insgesamt.

title: Gesundheit
description: Das körperliche und geistige Wohlbefinden umfasst viele Aspekte. Hier bündeln wir alle Inhalte zum Thema Gesundheit: Ob Medizin, Gesundheitspolitik, Ernährung oder Lebensweise.

title: Washington D.C.
description: Washington D.C. Ist Hauptstadt und Machtzentrum der Vereinigten Staaten. Die Abkürzung D.C. Steht für District of Columbia - einer alten Umschreibung für die USA. Das macht klar: Die Stadt gehört zu keinem Bundesstaat.

title: Iran-Krieg
description: Der Krieg begann Ende Februar mit Angriffen der USA und Israels auf den Iran. Auch andere Länder in der Region wurden von dem Konflikt in Mitleidenschaft gezogen.

title: Orthodoxes Christentum in Europa
description: Über 25 Millionen orthodoxe Christen leben in Europa. In Deutschland gehören rund vier Millionen Gläubige verschiedenen orthodoxen Kirchen an, darunter der rumänischen, griechischen und serbischen Kirche.

title: Öl, Gas, Strom: Iran-Krieg erschüttert die Weltwirtschaft
description: Die Blockade der Straße von Hormus trifft die weltweite Wirtschaft ins Mark. Produktionsausfälle und Engpässe bei Düngemitteln, Öl, Gas sowie gestiegene Energiepreise sind die Folge.

title: Nach der Ungarn-Wahl
description: In Ungarn hat sich ein Machtwechsel vollzogen. Nach 16 Jahren Orban-Regierung hat Oppositionsführer Peter Magyar mit seiner Tisza-Partei die Wahl gewonnen.

title: Weltraumflug zum Mond
description: Drei Männer, eine Frau, ein Ziel: Nach mehr als 50 Jahren fliegen wieder Menschen zum Mond. Auf der "Artemis 2"-Mission sollen sie in zehn Tagen zum Erdtrabanten und zurück fliegen. Die Faszination Mond ist ungebrochen.

title: Katherina Reiche
description: Die CDU-Politikerin Katherina Reiche ist seit dem 6. Mai 2025 Bundesministerin für Wirtschaft und Energie der Bundesrepublik Deutschland.

title: Hantavirus
description: Das Hantavirus ist eine Zoonose. Menschen stecken sich bei erkrankten Tieren durch Kontakt mit Exkrementen oder Speichel an. Symptome reichen von Fieber und Gliederschmerzen bis zu Nierenversagen und schwerer Atemnot.

title: Katholikentag
description: Der Katholikentag ist eine mehrtägige Zusammenkunft römisch-katholischer Christen in Deutschland, die in einem mehrjährigen Turnus stattfindet.

title: Bärbel Bas
description: Bärbel Bas war bis zu ihrem Rücktritt im Oktober 2026 Co-Vorsitzende der Sozialdemokratischen Partei Deutschlands (SPD) und Bundesarbeitsministerin.

title: Christopher Street Day (CSD)
description: CSDs sind Events für die Rechte der LGBTQ-Bewegung sowie gegen Diskriminierung und Ausgrenzung. Die Demos sind oft auch Paraden. Der Name CSD erinnert an schwule Aufstände in der New Yorker Christopher Street 1969.

title: Mark Carney
description: Mark Joseph Carney ist seit März 2025 Vorsitzender der Liberalen Partei Kanadas und Premierminister in dem nordamerikanischen Staat. Zuvor war er bereits Gouverneur der Bank of Canada und später Chef der Bank of England.

title: Landtagswahlen in Deutschland
description: In drei Bundesländern wurden im September neue Landesparlamente gewählt: Berlin, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern und Sachsen-Anhalt. Die Ergebnisse haben auch bundespolitische Bedeutung.

title: Flávio Bolsonaro
description: Der Sohn von Brasiliens Ex-Präsident Jair Bolsonaro tritt gegen Amtsinhaber Lula an. Der rechtspopulistische Kandidat will im Falle eines Wahlsieges seinen wegen Putschversuch verurteilten Vater begnadigen.

title: Сотни тысяч французов вновь вышли на протесты: задержаны более 1300 человек
description: Несмотря на усиленные меры безопасности и задержания, на протесты против роста стоимости жизни по всей Франции вновь вышли сотни тысяч человек. В ряде городов произошли столкновения с полицией.

title: Angela Merkel
description: Angela Merkel was Germany's first female chancellor, in office from 2005 to 2021, and leader of the center-right Christian Democratic Union from 2000 to 2018.

title: Bundesliga
description: The Bundesliga is Germany's top-flight professional football league. The men's 18-team league kicked off more than 60 years ago, in 1963, while the women's, formed in 1990, has 14 teams.

title: Auto industry
description: For more than a hundred years, carmakers have boosted economic growth, giving workers good jobs and shareholders healthy profits. Now, the industry is under pressure to transform amid climate change.

title: Nobel Peace Prize
description: Nobel Peace Prize laureates have included politicians, international organizations, peace movements and human rights advocates.

title: Sigmar Gabriel
description: Sigmar Gabriel is a German politician who served as Minister for Foreign Affairs, Vice-Chancellor of Germany from and was chairman of the Social Democratic Party (SPD).

title: Frank-Walter Steinmeier
description: Frank-Walter Steinmeier is a German politician who has served as Germany's president since 2017.

title: Joachim Löw
description: Former men's national football team head coach Joachim Löw guided Germany to their fourth World Cup title in Brazil in 2014.

title: Bayern Munich
description: Bayern Munich are Germany's most successful football club and one of Europe's most dominant teams. The club also excels in basketball and women's football.

title: Energiewende (transition to renewable power sources)
description: Germany's ambitions to completely restructure its energy sector have been talked about so much that the very word which stands for the current policy change — 'Energiewende' — has even made it into the English language.

title: Christian Democratic Union (CDU)
description: Germany's strongest political party, currently headed by Friedrich Merz, was in power for most of the time since the end of World War II.

title: Champions League
description: The UEFA Champions League is Europe's top club competition and one of the most prestigious in world football.

title: Borussia Dortmund
description: Borussia Dortmund are one of Germany's most successful clubs. They often play in the Champions League and their average attendance is among the highest in club football.

title: European Central Bank (ECB)
description: The European Central Bank monitors the monetary policy of the eurozone, with the main objective being to maintain price stability.

title: Michael Schumacher
description: Seven times Formula One world champion Michael Schumacher is one Germany's most famous sports stars.

title: G20 (Group of 20)
description: The Group of 20 is a collection of leading economic nations that account for roughly two-thirds of the world population and 80% of world trade.

title: Roma in Europe
description: With an estimated population of 10 million, the Roma are Europe's largest minority group. They are also among the poorest in most European countries and are often discriminated against.

title: Philippines
description: The Republic of the Philippines in Southeast Asia is an island country made up of more than 7,000 islands and islets. With a population of roughly 113 million, the ethnically diverse country has 19 recognized languages.

title: DFB Pokal (German Cup)
description: The DFB-Pokal, often referred to in English as the German Cup, is Germany's top cup competition. On the men's side it was first awarded in 1935; the women's tournament was first played out in the 1980-81 season.

title: FDP (Free Democratic Party)
description: Founded in 1948, the neoliberal Free Democrats frequently served as the junior coalition partner in German governments led by the CDU and the SPD.

title: Germany's Green Party
description: Bündnis 90/Die Grünen, Germany's Green party, was founded in West Germany in 1980 with an environmentalist and pacifist platform. Since the 2021 election, it has been a coalition partner in the federal government.

title: Frankfurt Book Fair
description: Germany's biggest annual book fair.

title: Joachim Gauck
description: Former German president, Joachim Gauck was a protestant pastor in East Germany before reunification.

title: World War II
description: World War II started with Nazi Germany's invasion of Poland in September 1939 and ended in Europe on May 8, 1945. In Asia, the war ended on August 15, 1945, following the atomic bombing of Japan's Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

title: Bundeswehr
description: Germany's military is one of the largest in Europe. "The Bundeswehr" is a catch-all term in German, encompassing the army, navy and air force.

title: Deutsche Bank
description: "Deutsche Bank" translates as "German Bank" and is a German global banking and financial services company with its headquarters in Frankfurt.

title: Bundesbank
description: Germany's central bank, headquartered in Frankfurt, is independent of the government.

title: OECD (Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development)
description: The OECD is an international economic organization of 38 countries, which regularly publishes reports analyzing and comparing economic policies of its member nations.

title: Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN)
description: The organization, which includes Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand, was founded in 1967 to improve cooperation in a region where the US and China are competing for influence.

title: Social Democratic Party (SPD)
description: Germany’s oldest party was founded in 1875, and is described as "center-left". It roots in the 19th century labor movement.

title: Christian Social Union (CSU)
description: The conservative CSU is a regional German party based in Bavaria, which plays an important role on the federal level as 'sister party' to the Christian Democrat CDU.

title: Left Party
description: Germany's socialist Left Party (Die Linke) is the most left-wing party in German post-reunification politics. It is the successor East Germany's ruling SED.

title: Helmut Kohl
description: Helmut Kohl (1930-2017) served as Chancellor of Germany from 1982 to 1998 and as the chairman of the Christian Democratic Union (CDU) from 1973 to 1998.

title: Barack Obama
description: Barack Obama was elected as the first African American president of the United States in 2008, and won reelection for a second term in 2012. In 2009, the first year he took office, he also received the Nobel Peace Prize.

title: European Union (EU)
description: The European Union is a economic and political association of 27 countries in Europe. The European Parliament meets to debate and vote on laws in Strasbourg, but Brussels is home to most of the European institutions.

title: United Nations (UN)
description: The UN has 193 members. Its objectives include promoting human rights, fostering social and economic development, protecting the environment, humanitarian aid and providing peacekeeping missions.

title: Berlin Wall
description: This year marks 65 years since East Germany's Socialist-ruled government began construction on the Berlin Wall. It cut off West Berlin from East Berlin and surrounded East Germany.

title: International Criminal Court (ICC)
description: The ICC is a permanent international tribunal to prosecute individuals for genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes. It is intended to complement existing national judicial systems.

title: International Court of Justice (ICJ)
description: The International Court of Justice is often commonly referred to as the world court. It's the primary judicial branch of the United Nations, based in The Hague. It mainly settles legal disputes submitted to it by states.

title: Gregor Gysi
description: Gregor Gysi is a trained attorney and veteran politician of Germany's socialist Left Party.

title: Volkswagen
description: German carmaking giant Volkswagen is reeling from a massive sales and cost crisis and falling profits. It says it plans to scrap four plants and up to 100.000 jobs in Germany.

title: Bayerische Motorenwerke (BMW)
description: BMW is one of Germany's top automobile, motorcycle and engine manufacturing companies. By model sales, its main BMW badge is in the top 15 car manufacturers on the planet.

title: Dalai Lama
description: The Dalai Lama is the head monk of the Gelugpa lineage of Tibetan Buddhism. The 14th Dalai Lama, he won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1989.

title: International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)
description: The IAEA is an international organization that seeks to promote the peaceful use of nuclear technology. It aims to prevent its use for any military purpose.

title: Vladimir Putin
description: Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin has been serving as President of Russia since 2012.

title: Xi Jinping
description: Xi Jinping, born in 1953, was elected president and head of China's ruling Communist Party in 2013. In March 2023, he was awarded an unprecedented third term.

title: Pope Francis
description: Jorge Mario Bergoglio, born in Buenos Aires in 1936, was elected head of the Catholic Church in 2013 after the resignation of his predecessor, Pope Benedict. His papacy centered on peace, inclusion and the environment.

title: United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF)
description: UNICEF is a United Nations institution that provides long-term humanitarian and developmental assistance to children and mothers in developing countries.

title: World War I
description: World War I started with the shot heard around the world: the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria on July 28, 1914, in Sarajevo. By 1918, more than 9 million people had died and Europe's map was redrawn.

title: Eurovision Song Contest
description: The Eurovision Song Contest is an annual singing competition held among the European Broadcasting Union member countries since 1956. Traditionally held in May, the format comprises two semifinals and a grand final.

title: Oktoberfest
description: Oktoberfest is an annual folk festival held in Munich in the southern German state of Bavaria. It's the largest beer festival in the world, attracting some 6-7 million visitors from across the world.

title: National Security Agency (NSA)
description: The National Security Agency (NSA) is the main US agency for global monitoring, collection, decoding, translation and analysis of foreign intelligence data.

title: Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC)
description: APEC is a forum for economic cooperation of all countries bordering the Pacific. It was set up in 1989 in response to the economic rise of Asian countries.

title: Helmut Schmidt
description: Helmut Schmidt (1918-2015) was described as one of the most respected German politicians of all time — and the country’s most prominent chain smoker.

title: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
description: The International Monetary Fund groups 190 countries; its aim is to secure financial stability.

title: Press freedom
description: A free and independent media landscape, a fundamental characteristic of democracies, is protected by the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

title: Edward Snowden
description: Edward Snowden, a former US intelligence contractor, made headlines on June 5, 2013 with his disclosure of classified information on global surveillance by the NSA. The leak shone the spotlight on data protection.

title: Martin Schulz
description: Martin Schulz is a German politician from the SPD. He heads the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats and was president of the European Parliament until 2017.

title: European Parliament
description: The European Parliament currently has 720 members, who are elected every five years by universal suffrage. It meets in Strasbourg and in Brussels and also has offices in Luxembourg.

title: European Commission
description: The European Commission is the executive body of the European Union. It is primarily based in Brussels.

title: Women's rights
description: Women's rights are protected in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. They include the right to bodily integrity, suffrage, the right to education, work, equal pay, the right to hold public office and own property.

title: Human rights
description: Human rights are moral principles which apply to all humans. At least in theory, they apply to all humans equally, anywhere in the world.

title: LGBTQ+ rights
description: LGBTQ+ rights are human and civil rights, but the rights of lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and queer people vary worldwide. In June and July, LGBTQ+ people and their allies across the globe celebrate Pride.

title: Architecture
description: Architecture is part of a country’s cultural identity. This refers to the planning, designing, and constructing of a wide range of buildings.

title: Pirate Party
description: The Pirate Party rose to popularity in Germany in 2011, but then got embroiled in in-fighting and failed to convince voters to elect them into parliament in the 2013 general election.

title: Alternative for Germany (AfD)
description: Germany's far-right populist Alternative for Germany, or AfD, is the second-largest party in Germany's parliament.

title: Genetic engineering (GMO)
description: Genetic engineering is the direct modification or manipulation of an organism's genome using biotechnology. The result is a genetically modified organism, or GMO.

title: African Union (AU)
description: The African Union (AU) is a union consisting of 55 African states. Its goal is to promote political and economic cooperation on the continent.

title: The Oscars
description: The Academy Awards, also known as the Oscars, are Hollywood's most high-profile award ceremony for the cinema industry. They have been presented every year since 1929 by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences.

title: Technology
description: Technological advances from artificial intelligence, robotics, and medical devices are rapidly changing the world and how we use them for practical purposes.

title: Top 10 lists
description: Take a look at our most popular top 10 lists. You'll find everything from German idioms and kitschy souvenirs to the most polluted places on earth and the biggest stories of the year.

title: Scene in Berlin
description: What's the hot topic of discussion in Berlin, what's the trend on the streets? DW's Berlin columnists bring you a weekly insider's perspective on culture, lifestyle and society in the German capital.

title: Archaeology
description: Read more about research, excavation and preservation of archaeological sites and cultural heritage.

title: Flight MH370
description: Flight MH370 disappeared without a trace on May 8th, 2014

title: Flight MH17
description: Malaysia Airline Flight MH17 was an international flight carrying 298 people. On July 17, 2014 the plane was shot down while flying above eastern Ukraine, killing all on board.

title: Cornelius Gurlitt
description: A German art collector who was discovered to possess 1,500 artworks believed to have been stolen by the Nazis from their rightful Jewish owners during World War II.

title: Oscar Pistorius
description: South African Paralympian and double amputee Oscar Pistorius has been banned from competition since 2013 while a court investigated his role in the fatal shooting of his girlfriend, Reeva Steenkamp.

title: Germany's Federal Constitutional Court
description: Germany's Federal Constitutional Court (BVG, or Bundesverfassungsgericht) is the country's high court, its main task being judicial review.

title: David Cameron
description: The UK's prime minister from 2010 until 2016. Cameron led the Conservative party for more than a decade. He is best known for calling the referendum on EU membership, campaigning to remain, losing, and then quitting.

title: Ban Ki-moon
description: Ban Ki-moon was the eighth secretary-general of the United Nations.

title: Cannes International Film Festival
description: The Cannes Film Festival, founded in France in 1946, has become one of the world's most prestigious cinema events.

title: 'Islamic State' group
description: The 'Islamic State' group is an extremist organization

title: Boko Haram
description: Boko Haram is a militant Islamist movement most active in northeastern Nigeria. The group also has footholds in Chad, Niger, Cameroon, and Mali. One of its stated goals is to introduce Sharia law across its territory.

title: Charlie Hebdo
description: "Charlie Hebdo" is a French satirical weekly magazine, published in Paris since 1992. In 2006, it was among the few publications which reprinted Muhammad caricatures first seen in the Danish paper "Jyllands-Posten."

title: Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi
description: Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi is the leader of the self-named terror organization "Islamic State" (IS).

title: Raif Badawi
description: Raif Badawi is a Saudi Arabian human rights activist and blogger. In November 2014 he was sentenced to ten years in prison, a fine and 1000 lashes for insulting Islam.

title: Arab Spring
description: The Arab Spring was a series of protests directed against various authoritarian regimes in the Middle East, starting at the end of 2010.

title: Sarah's Music
description: “Sarah’s Music – Contemporary Classical” is DW’s monthly program dedicated to the rich diversity of classical music. Presenter Sarah Willis gets up close and personal with the stars of the classical music world.

title: Munich Security Conference
description: The annual Munich Security Conference brings together security experts and politicians, military leaders and the defense industry from around the world.

title: Literature
description: Books and other forms of writing are fundamental ways we express ourselves. Literature is our way of preserving knowledge, and it can have both political and societal impacts.

title: Germanwings 4U 9525 crash
description: Germanwings flight 4U 9525 crashed in the French Alps on March 24, 2015, en route from Barcelona to Düsseldorf, killing all 150 people onboard. This was the German carrier's worst accident to date.

title: Günter Grass
description: Günter Grass was a German writer. Born in Danzig in 1927, he is best known for his first novel, The Tin Drum (Die Blechtrommel, 1959).

title: Basketball
description: Basketball is the most globally popular American sport, the NBA and WNBA are the world's top leagues. The sport is also played in Europe (EuroLeague), Africa (BAL) and on the international stage (FIBA World Cup)

title: UNESCO World Heritage
description: More than 1,000 sites around the world have been identified by UNESCO as being of special value to humanity. These locations, of both natural and cultural significance, are given special protection and attention.

title: Climate change
description: Increased levels of carbon dioxide and other human-caused emissions being released into the atmosphere have pushed global surface and ocean temperatures to rise at unprecedented speed.

title: Schengen area
description: The area comprises 29 European countries that have abolished internal border controls. Implemented in 1995, it resembles a single state for international travel purposes with external border controls and common visas.

title: Dieselgate
description: German carmaker Volkswagen has admitted to rigging millions of diesel vehicles worldwide in a bid to thwart emissions tests in the US and elsewhere.

title: Afghanistan
description: The Islamic Republic of Afghanistan has been under Taliban rule since August 2021, following the withdrawal of US and NATO-allied troops.

title: Julian Assange
description: Julian Assange, an Australian editor and publisher, is best best known for founding the anti-secrecy website WikiLeaks, responsible for the 2010 release of a trove of US classified documents.

title: Aung San Suu Kyi
description: Myanmar's prominent opposition leader led the National League for Democracy (NLD) party to win the 2015 general election.

title: Alzheimer's disease
description: Estimated to account for up to 70 percent of dementia cases, Alzheimer's is a severe neurodegenerative disease.

title: Arab League
description: The Arab League is a regional organization of countries in the Middle East and North Africa.

title: Mobile World Congress
description: Each year, the Mobile World Congress brings together enthusiasts from the digital world sharing their view on the latest gadgets.

title: Geneva Motor Show
description: From the first car exhibition in Switzerland in 1905 to the international event of nowadays, the Geneva International Motor Show is one of the top five events in the industry worldwide not to be missed.

title: Industry 4.0
description: Industry 4.0 is often called the fourth industrial revolution. The term embraces a number of modern automation, data exchange and manufacturing technologies.

title: North Korea
description: Under its totalitarian leader Kim Jong Un, North Korea is mostly ostracized from the international community. The country and its neighbor South Korea are in constant conflict, which occasionally heats up.

title: Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus
description: The Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus is a self-declared state that comprises the northeastern portion of the island of Cyprus. The TRNC is internationally recognized only by Turkey.

title: North Rhine-Westphalia
description: North Rhine-Westphalia (NRW) is the most populous federal state in Germany. The biggest metropolitan area of the European continent, Rhine-Ruhr, is located within the state.

title: New Zealand
description: New Zealand is an island country in the southwestern Pacific Ocean. It is situated some 1,500 kilometers east of Australia across the Tasman Sea.

title: Muhammadu Buhari
description: President of Nigeria, took office in May 2015, after defeating Goodluck Jonathan in elections. Born December 17, 1942, Muhammadu Buhari is part of the All Progressives Congress party.

title: Jeremy Corbyn
description: Labour Party politician in the UK, Member of Parliament for Islington North (in London) since 1983, voted Labour leader after the party's defeat in the 2015 general elections.

title: The Walt Disney Co.
description: Multinational mass media and entertainment conglomerate specializing in Mickey Mouse, movies, merchandise, theme parks, television, radio, music, publishing and more.

title: European Space Agency (ESA)
description: Intergovernmental space exploration agency with 22 member states, established on May 30, 1975. The organization's 2023 budget was around 4.9 billion euros.

title: Alexander Gerst
description: PhD geophysicist who studied in Karlsruhe, New Zealand and Hamburg; Alexander Gerst is a German astronaut who was part of the International Space Station crew from May to November 2014.

title: Marine Le Pen
description: Marine Le Pen, a lawyer by profession, is the former president of France's nationalist right-wing National Rally (RN), having led the party from 2011 to 2021. She ran for president in 2012, 2017 and 2022.

title: Mergers & Acquisitions
description: 2015 was a record year for corporate mergers, with huge transaction sums involved in the takeover bids.

title: IPO (initial public offering)
description: Going public for a company means first of all to be able to raise fresh capital. But an initial public offering can end in disaster, too.

title: World Bank
description: The World Bank serves as an international financial institution granting loans to developing countries. The recipients have to pledge structural reforms in return.

title: Electric vehicles
description: A boost in electric vehicle manufacturing has occurred due to advances in batteries and energy management. But are the vehicles still too expensive to become a major global hit?

title: US Federal Reserve
description: The Federal Reserve is the United States' central bank. It's played a pivotal role in guiding the US through the global financial crisis through its low-interest monetary policy.

title: Amnesty International
description: Amnesty International (commonly known as Amnesty and AI) is a non-governmental organisation focused on human rights. It was founded in London in 1961.

title: Kofi Annan
description: Kofi Annan was Secretary-General of the United Nations from 1997 until 2006. In 2001 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize with the United Nations.

title: Baden-Württemberg
description: Baden-Württemberg is a state located in Germany's southwest. It is Germany’s third largest state in terms of size and population, with an area of 35,742 square kilometres (13,800 sq mi) and 10.7 million inhabitants.

title: Bayer Leverkusen
description: In 2023-24 Bayer Leverkusen secured the first Bundesliga title in club history, ending Bayern Munich's 11-year run. They completed the double by winning their second German Cup after 1993.

title: Schleswig-Holstein
description: Schleswig-Holstein is the northernmost of the 16 states of Germany, comprising most of the historical duchy of Holstein and the southern part of the former Duchy of Schleswig. Its capital city is Kiel.

title: Lower Saxony
description: Lower Saxony is Germany's second largest federal state, situated in the northwest with a population of 8 million.This is where the German environmentalist movement began in protest against nuclear waste disposal.

title: Rhineland-Palatinate
description: Rhineland-Palatinate is one of the 16 states of the Federal Republic of Germany. It has a population of four million. The city of Mainz is the state capital.

title: Saxony-Anhalt
description: The Alternative for Germany (AfD) party has won the Saxony-Anhalt state election. The result is a historic victory for the anti-immigration party and a symbolic blow to German Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

title: Brandenburg
description: Brandenburg is one of Germany's 16 federal states and surrounds the capital, Berlin, but does not include it. It has a population of just under 6 million.

title: Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania
description: Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, also known as Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, is a state in northeastern Germany. The capital city is Schwerin. The state is located in a region that used to be part of former East Germany.

title: Environment
description: Plants and animals, but also soil, water and climate — the environment is all around us, and we depend on it to survive.

title: Conservation
description: From saving threatened and endangered plants and animals to establishing and managing biosphere reserves and protected areas, conservation is about protecting species and ecosystems.

title: Sameh Shoukry
description: Sameh Shoukry is the current Egyptian Foreign Minister.

title: Agriculture
description: In many parts of the world, agriculture has been marked by increased productivity. And yet, that alone has not been enough to eradicate global hunger.

title: Xenophobia
description: Xenophobia is the fear of everything perceived to be foreign or strange. It affects the relations and perceptions of groups of people toward another one.

title: Fatou Bensouda
description: Fatou Bensouda is the chief prosecutor at the International Criminal Court (ICC).

title: Zika virus
description: Zika, well known in Latin American and Caribbean countries, is known to cause birth defects such as microcephaly if pregnant women become infected. It is often transmitted by mosquitoes.

title: Renewable energy
description: Whether wind, solar or hydropower — renewable energy is booming worldwide. Sun, wind, water, biogas and biomass are readily available and can sustainably supply us with clean energy.

title: Social media
description: Social media, like Instagram, TikTok, Facebook and WhatsApp, has become an integral part of our lives, bringing both pros and cons.

title: Extreme weather
description: Heavy flooding, severe storms, record heat waves — climate change has brought an increase in the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events. People, ecosystems and global economies are suffering the consequences.

title: Global food security
description: The combined impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, climate change and the war in Ukraine has resulted in rising food prices and an acute shortage in staple crops globally. Millions of people are now on the verge of hunger.

title: Deutsche Bahn
description: Founded in 1994, Germany's state-owned national rail operator, Deutsche Bahn, covers regional, national and international passenger and cargo routes. The company employs more than 300,000 people.

title: Employment
description: Jobs provide most people with their main source of income, should they not be in a lucky position to earn more in terms of capital revenues. But being employed is also about social inclusion.

title: Deforestation
description: Much of the world used to be covered with trees. But most of the world's ancient forests have been cut down.

title: Heat and drought
description: Extreme heat, droughts and wildfires are becoming increasingly common as global temperatures rise and rain and snowmelt decline.

title: Pina Bausch
description: German dancer and choreographer Pina Bausch influenced the field of modern dance like hardly any other, developing the Tanztheater technique of blending dance with dramatic elements.

title: Solar power
description: The sun provides free energy for the taking in the form of photovoltaic or concentrated solar power. It's a big business that can help save our climate. But to what extent is this being used?

title: Dimitris Avramopoulos
description: Dimitris Avramopoulos is a Greek politician who has served as Minister of Foreign Affairs and Minister of National Defense. He currently acts as the European Commissioner for Migration, Home Affairs and Citizenship.

title: East Germany (GDR)
description: Declared in 1949, the German Democratic Republic was a Socialist-run state in the Soviet-occupied east after World War II. Following protests in 1989, the GDR ceased to exist with the reunification of Germany in 1990.

title: Wind power
description: Across the world, wind has been used to harness energy for centuries. Modern wind turbines are even more efficient and work both on land and in offshore wind parks.

title: Hydropower
description: Hydropower is supposed to be 'clean,' as it doesn't rely on the burning of fossil fuels. But this form of renewable energy is controversial for several reasons.

title: Natural resources
description: Whether precious minerals like gold or fossil fuels like coal, the Earth yields a bounty - and often suffers for it.

title: #WhatAmerica
description: During the US presidential campaign, DW has been asking voters what kind of America they want for the future. Now it's taking that question to the world.

title: United States of America
description: The United States remains the world’s largest economy, while domestic debate over the conflict and the president’s war powers has intensified during Donald Trump's second term.

title: Berlin Fashion Week
description: Taking place twice yearly, in January and July, Berlin Fashion Week showcases ready-to-wear styles in both fashion shows and an industry fair.

title: Ludwig van Beethoven
description: The German composer (1770-1827) is one of the most influential composers of all time and played an important role in the transition from the Classical to Romantic eras in European classical music.

title: Switzerland
description: Switzerland, a wealthy Alpine state in Central Europe, was founded in 1291 and has four official languages. Its system of government is based on direct democracy and a tradition of political and military neutrality.

title: Johann Sebastian Bach
description: During his lifetime, German composer Johann Sebastian Bach (1685-1750) was considered an outstanding organist. But only posthumously did he come to be revered as one of the most significant composers of all time.

title: George Clooney
description: George Clooney, born in 1961 in Lexington, Kentucky, is one of Hollywood's most outstanding actors, but also a director, producer and screenwriter.

title: Bashar Assad
description: Bashar Assad was Syria's president from 2000-2024 before rebel groups removed him from power. Assad's regime conducted a violent crackdown of protests in 2011 that led to the Syrian Civil War.

title: Gerhard Schröder
description: Born in 1944, the Social Democrat was Germany's chancellor from 1998 to 2005. After his term in office, Schröder became best known for the close ties he forged with Russia and its oil and gas industry.

title: Gaza Strip
description: Palestinians continue to suffer in war-ravaged Gaza despite an Israel-Hamas ceasefire deal, which began in October 2025.

title: Sigmar Polke
description: Sigmar Polke (1941-2010) was a German artist who, during various phases of his life, focused on photography and painting and played an important role in the development of modern art.

title: Sustainability
description: Insisting on sustainability in the economy means first of all to make sure that current production methods do not compromise the ability of the generations to come to shape their own future.

title: Berlinale Talents
description: Every February Berlinale Talents brings 300 selected talents (writers, directors, producers, cinematographers, actors, editors etc) together with professionals from the international film industry.

title: Scooter (band)
description: Scooter, fronted by H.P. Baxxter, are a highly successful dance/trance group originating from Hamburg in Germany. The group, founded in 1993, has sold over 30 million records.

title: Urban farming
description: Agriculture in the city: Be it rooftop gardens or highly efficient hydroponics, urban farming makes cities a little "greener" and helps feed their residents. And the projects come in all different sizes.

title: Bishop Bernard Fellay
description: Bishop Bernard Fellay is the Superior General of The Society of St. Pius X.

title: Berlin Philharmonic
description: The Berlin Philharmonic (Berliner Philharmoniker), founded in Berlin in 1882, is considered one of the 10 best orchestras in the world.

title: General Motors
description: General Motors is an iconic American auto manufacturer headquartered in Detroit, Michigan. A Fortune 500 company, it has some of the most recognizable brands in the industry, including Chevrolet, Cadillac and Buick.

title: Lucas Cranach, the Elder
description: Lucas Cranach, the Elder (1472-1553), was a German painter of the Renaissance era who produced altarpieces, woodcuts and engravings. Even during his lifetime, he was considered the most outstanding artist of his time.

title: Lucas Cranach, the Younger
description: Lucas Cranach, the Younger (1515-1586), son of Lucas Cranach, the Elder, remained in the shadow of his famous father throughout his career, during which he predominantly created new versions of his father's paintings.

title: Anne Frank
description: One of the most widely discussed victims of the Holocaust, Anne Frank is best known for the diary she composed while hiding from the Nazis in an Amsterdam apartment.

title: Deutsche Telekom
description: Deutsche Telekom is a German telecoms giant headquartered in Bonn. The former state telephone monopolist has recently been able to log decent earnings despite fierce competition.

title: Valdis Dombrovskis
description: Valdis Dombrovskis is the European Commissioner for the Euro and Social Dialogue. He served as Prime Minister of Latvia from 2009 until 2014.

title: Nicolas Sarkozy
description: Nicolas Sarkozy was born in 1955 to a Hungarian immigrant father. A leading figure in France's center right, he served as president from 2007 to 2012.

title: Recep Tayyip Erdogan
description: Born in 1954, Recep Tayyip Erdogan served as prime minister of Turkey from 2003 to 2014. He became the country's first president to be elected by popular vote in 2014.

title: Palestinian territories
description: The occupied Gaza Strip and West Bank, including east Jerusalem, make up the Palestinian territories.

title: Commerzbank
description: Commerzbank is Germany's second-largest bank with offices in more than 50 countries. It finances about 30 percent of German foreign trade and is the unchallenged leader in financing for small and mid-sized enterprises..

title: DAX (and other stock markets)
description: The DAX is Germany's primary stock index, listing the 40 largest companies that trade on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange. The acronym stands for Deutscher Aktienindex, or German stock index.

title: ThyssenKrupp
description: ThyssenKrupp is a German industrial engineering and steel production conglomerate created in a merger of Thyssen AG and Krupp. It claims to be one of the world's largest steel, Here is some DW content on the company.

title: Mining and minerals
description: Extracting minerals can bring a range of benefits, but mines can also provoke conflict and harm people and the environment.

title: German economy
description: Germany's economy is highly advanced and the largest in Europe. On a global scale it is the third-biggest. Germany's top-five exports are vehicles, machinery, chemical goods, electronic products and electrical equipment.

title: Franz Marc
description: German painter Franz Marc (1880-1916) was a foremost representative of the German Expressionist movement. He also co-founded the artists' group "Blue Rider," together with Wassily Kandinsky and August Macke.

title: Svetlana Alexievich
description: Belarusian writer Svetlana Alexievich was born 1948 in Ukraine, and writes in Russian. In 2015, she was awarded the Literature Nobel Prize for her "polyphonic writings, a monument to suffering and courage in our time."

title: Nikolaus Harnoncourt
description: In a career spanning six decades, he was one of the most influential conductors of the 20th and early 21st centuries.

title: Turkey-Syria earthquake 2023
description: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck Turkey and Syria on February 6, 2023: More than 56,000 people were kileld and hundreds of thousands displaced.

title: Wassily Kandinsky
description: Russian artist Wassily Kandinsky (1866-1944) was both an influential painter and art theorist, who is credited with developing abstract art.

title: Frauke Petry
description: Frauke Petry chaired the far-right lternative für Deutschland (AfD) party from 2015 to 2017.

title: The Netherlands
description: The Netherlands is a small country located in western Europe with three island territories in the Caribbean. Its capital is Amsterdam.

title: Bruno Ganz
description: Best known for depicting Hitler, Bruno Ganz is considered one of the most important contemporary actors of German-language cinema.

title: Pussy Riot
description: The Russian feminist punk rock protest group became famous through their guerrilla performance in a Moscow Church that led to the arrest of some of the members of the band.

title: Hans Zimmer
description: He is one of Hollywood's most successful Composers of film scores. German music producer Hans Zimmer has worked on over 150 movies, from "Rain Man" to "The Dark Knight Trilogy," and has won an Oscar for "The Lion King."

title: Roger Cicero
description: Roger Cicero was one of Germany's best-known jazz performers. His career spanned almost 15 years, making him one of Germany's most beloved musical celebrities. He died in March 2016 at the young age of 45.

title: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart
description: Austrian-German genius composer Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (1756-1791) will likely be eternally admired for the inimitable pristine clarity and divinely harmonious melodies of his music - plus the sheer volume of his work.

title: Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK)
description: The PKK was a militant Kurdish organization, designated as a terrorist group by Turkey, the United States and the European Union. It launched its armed struggle in the 1980s but disbanded in 2025.

title: Bundestag (Germany's lower house of parliament)
description: The "Bundestag" is Germany's main legislative body. Its over members are elected every four years in a mixed system of constituency and list voting.

title: Saudi Arabia
description: Saudi Arabia, the largest Middle Eastern country, is among the world's top oil producers and home to Islam's holiest city, Mecca. Run by Prince Mohammed bin Salman, it is often criticized for its human rights record.

title: Panama Papers
description: The leak of 11.5 million documents from the Panama-based service provider Mossack Fonseca, once the world's fourth-biggest offshore law firm, shows how some of the world's most famous use tax havens to hide their wealth.

title: Herbert Grönemeyer
description: Herbert Grönemeyer is one of Germany's most popular musicians.

title: Jan Böhmermann
description: Jan Böhmermann is a German satirist, radio and TV personality who was born in Bremen in 1981. In 2016, one of his poems about Turkey's president led to diplomatic tensions between Turkey and Germany.

title: Taylor Swift
description: Taylor Swift is an American singer and songwriter who was born in Pennsylvania in 1989. She began her music career as a country singer, but she is now one of the most popular pop stars in the world.

title: Queen Elizabeth II
description: Elizabeth Alexandra Mary was the queen of the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia and New Zealand, as well as the head of the Commonwealth. She was born in 1926 and died on September 8, 2022.

title: William Shakespeare
description: William Shakespeare was an English poet and playwright who was born in Stratford-upon-Avon in 1564. His works consist of approximately 38 plays,154 sonnets and two long narrative poems.

title: Prince Rogers Nelson
description: En route to becoming the most prolific pop star of his period, Prince Rogers Nelson (June 7, 1958-April 21, 2016) bent both gender and genre.

title: Game of Thrones
description: "Game of Thrones" is an American fantasy television series. It was created by David Benioff and D.B.Weiss, and is based on the novels by George R. R. Martin, the first of which is called "A Game of Thrones."

title: Tom Tykwer
description: Tom Tykwer, born in Wuppertal in 1965, has worked as a film producer, director, screenwriter and composer. He is most internationally renowned for directing films like "Run Lola Run" and "Perfume:TheStory of a Murderer."

title: Follow the Hashtag
description: What makes a topic go viral? How do people respond to a trending hashtag? Can Twitter activism make a difference in real life? These are some of the questions DW addresses in the video series Follow the Hashtag.

title: Abu Sayyaf
description: Abu Sayyaf is an Islamist militant group in the Philippines which has carried out attacks since 1991. They are engaged in an insurgency for an independent province.

title: Cultural Revolution (China)
description: The "Great Proletarian Cultural Revolution" took place in the People's Republic of China from 1966 until 1976. It was started by Mao Zedong, then Chairman of the Communist Party of China.

title: Smartphone
description: A smartphone refers to a cellphone that combines the functions of a regular cellphone with features of a computer.

title: Green tech
description: Technology that sustains the environment. From renewable energy innovations to pollution solutions — smart green ideas are emerging now more than ever.

title: Kendrick Lamar
description: Kendrick Lamar Duckworth, born in Compton, California, in 1987, is a US rapper. He has received wide acclaim and a number of accolades over the course of his career, including seven Grammy Awards.

title: Washington, D.C.
description: Washington, D.C., is a US territory located between Maryland and Virginia. It was built between 1790 and 1800 to serve as the seat of the federal government.

title: John Kerry
description: John Forbes Kerry is an American diplomat and Democratic Party politician. Born in 1943, he started his political career in the early 1970s.

title: Benjamin Netanyahu
description: Benjamin Netanyahu is the current prime minister of Israel and chair of the right-wing conservative Likud party. Born in 1949, he is the first prime minister born in Israel after the establishment of the state.

title: Adolf Hitler
description: Adolf Hitler was the Nazi dictator who ruled Germany from 1933 to 1945. He initiated World War II and was the central figure responsible for the Holocaust.

title: The International Security Assistance Force (ISAF)
description: ISAF was a NATO-led security mission in Afghanistan, established by the United Nations in 2001. Its main purpose was to train the Afghan forces and assist in rebuilding government institutions.

title: Central Intelligence Agency, CIA
description: The Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) is a foreign intelligence service of the US Government. It is focused on overseas intelligence gathering and analyzing security information.

title: Justice and Development Party (AKP)
description: The Justice and Development Party is Turkey's largest political party. It was forged in 2001 by the merger of several conservative, Islamist and nationalist parties.The party is led by President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

title: Bundesnachrichtendienst, BND
description: The Federal Intelligence Service, BND, is the foreign intelligence agency of Germany. It alerts the German government to threats to German interests from abroad.

title: Northern Ireland
description: The smaller, northern segment of Ireland, the North Atlantic island. Northern Ireland is a part of the United Kingdom. Site of decades of conflict between British loyalists and Irish republicans, it has calmed of late.

title: Republic of Ireland
description: The Republic of Ireland is the larger portion of the island of Ireland. The smaller part is Northern Ireland, which belongs to the United Kingdom. The Republic of Ireland is a largely Catholic EU and eurozone member.

title: Smart home
description: Smart home technology keeps people connected with their living environments.

title: Kraftwerk (band)
description: Kraftwerk, founded by Ralf Hütter and Florian Schneider in Dusseldorf in 1970, is a German band known for being a pioneer of electronic music.

title: Harry Potter
description: Aspiring young wizard Harry Potter is the fictional protagonist in the best-selling book series in history, selling more than 400 million copies in numerous languages.

title: Marilyn Monroe
description: Marilyn Monroe (1926-1962), born and raised in Los Angeles as Norma Jeane Mortenson, was a famous Hollywood actress and very popular sex symbol who continues to be a major culture icon.

title: Yannick Nezet-Seguin
description: Yannick Nezet-Seguin, born in Montreal in 1975, is a Canadian conductor and pianist.

title: Led Zeppelin
description: Led Zeppelin were one of the most influential British rock bands founded in London in 1968.

title: Anja Niedringhaus
description: Anja Niedringhaus (1965-2014), was a German photojournalist and Pulitzer Prize winner who got killed in Afghanistan. The Anja Niedringhaus Courage in Photojournalism Award was created to honor her life and work.

title: Sarah Willis
description: Sarah Willis is a British hornist and a television presenter. Since 2014, she hosts the weekly music magazine "Sarah's Music" for DW.

title: Joan Miró
description: Joan Miró (1893-1983), born in Barcelona, was a Spanish painter, sculptor and ceramicist, and a leading representative of both Surrealism and Catalan nationalism.

title: Georg Baselitz
description: One of Germany's most renowned contemporary artists, Georg Baselitz is known for his works on Germany's past — and for deliberately showing some paintings upside down, demonstrating his penchant for variation and change.

title: Tate Modern
description: Tate Modern, located in central London, is Britain's national gallery of international modern and contemporary art and one of the most significant institutions of its kind in the world.

title: Michel Houellebecq
description: Michel Houellebecq, born Michel Thomas in Réunion in 1956, is a highly controversial French author, poet and filmmaker. He adopted his grandmother's maiden name Houellebecq as his pen name.

title: Roland Emmerich
description: Roland Emmerich, born in Stuttgart in 1955, is a German director, screenwriter and producer. Most of his blockbuster productions are catastrophe films like "Godzilla" (1998) and "Independence Day" (1996).

title: Götz George
description: Götz George (1938-2016) was a German actor best known for playing the detective Horst Schimanski in the highly successful German television crime series, "Tatort."

title: The Beatles
description: John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison and Ringo Starr made up what would become the most influential band of the rock era. The Beatles were founded in 1960 in Liverpool, England.

title: Mel Brooks
description: Mel Brooks is known as a master of parody. Born Melvin James Kaminsky in 1926 in New York, is a highly successful US comedian, filmmaker, actor, songwriter and composer.

title: Pasternak, Ben
description: Ben Pasternak is start-up founder who grew up in Sydney, Australia. He first achieved success with the game "Impossible Rush," which he developed at the age of 14. It has been downloaded millions of times.

title: Elie Wiesel
description: Eliezer "Elie" Wiesel (1928-2016) was a Romanian-born Holocaust survivor who later became a Nobel Prize-winning author, professor, and political activist.

title: Sylvester Stallone
description: Sylvester Stallone, born in 1946 in New York, is a US actor, screenwriter, producer, and director. He is best known for his roles in the "Rocky" and "Rambo" films from the 1980s and the more recent "Expendables" series.

title: Andreas Gursky
description: Andreas Gursky is a German photographer known for his digitally modified photos that critically examine consumerism and the ills of modern life. He was born in 1955 in Leipzig, but grew up in Dusseldorf.

title: Daniel Barenboim
description: Daniel Barenboim, born in 1942 in Buenos Aires, is a world renowned conductor and pianist. He is known for work with the West-Eastern Divan Orchestra, which brings together young Israeli and Arab musicians.

title: Digital Nomad
description: A digital nomad is a business owner or employee who works primarily with digital technology. Thanks to the internet, they can work anywhere.

title: Bayreuth Festival
description: The annual Bayreuth Festival is dedicated exclusively to the operatic works of German composer Richard Wagner. The five-week series of performances begins each year on July 25 in Bayreuth, Germany.

title: Salzburg Festival
description: The Salzburg Festival is one of the world's largest and in artistically most renowned festivals. Concert, opera and theater are its three central elements.

title: Frank Farian
description: Best known for founding the group Boney M. In the 19709s, Frank Farian is one of Germany's most successful music producers.

title: Melania Trump
description: Melania Trump, born Melanija Knavs in 1970 in Slovenia, is a former fashion model and wife of US President Donald Trump.

title: Humboldt Forum
description: The Humboldt Forum is a large-scale museum project in Berlin, located at the site of the City Palace. It is expected to open in 2019.

title: Rainer Werner Fassbinder
description: Rainer Werner Fassbinder (1945-1982) was a German director, film producer, author and actor, and a representative of the New German Film movement.

title: Vincent van Gogh
description: Vincent van Gogh (1853-1890) was a representative of the Dutch post-impressionism period and one of the world's best-known artists. He created more than 2,100 artworks in his short career, including 860 oil paintings.

title: Bolshoi Theater
description: Located in Moscow, the Bolshoi Theatre is the most significant location for ballet and opera in Russia. It is home to the Bolshoi Ballet and Bolshoi Opera companies.

title: Berners-Lee, Tim
description: Sir Timothy "Tim" John Berners-Lee, born on June 8, 1955 in London, is a British physicist and computer scientist. He became widely known as the inventor of the World Wide Web.

title: Shah Rukh Khan
description: The biggest name in Bollywood, Shah Rukh Khan has appeared in more than 80 movies and has become a household name the world over. Khan's career spanning 30 years has earned him numerous awards and accolades.

title: Donald Trump
description: In his second presidential term, Trump has further alienated traditional allies. As agents carry out his anti-immigration agenda, the US has arrested the president of Venezuela and made further threats toward Greenland.

title: SC Freiburg
description: Despite having been relegated more than once, Freiburg have established themselves as a mainstay in Germany's top flight since they were first promoted to the Bundesliga in 1993.

title: Locarno Film Festival
description: The Festival del Film Locarno has taken place annually in August in Locarno, Switzerland, since 1946. The film event is particularly known for its outdoor screening area at the Piazza Grande.

title: Wacken Open Air
description: Wacken Open Air is the world's biggest heavy metal music festival. The four-day event takes place each summer in the tiny village of Wacken northwest of Hamburg.

title: Brandenburg Gate
description: The Brandenburg Gate is one of the most significant landmarks in Berlin, symbolizing German and European history, as well as peace and unity.

title: Kanye West
description: Kanye West, now legally known as Ye, is an American rapper, musician, singer and music producer, who also works as a fashion designer. He has also used the pseudonym Yeezy.

title: Christoph Waltz
description: Christoph Waltz, born 1956 in Vienna, is an acclaimed actor with German and Austrian citizenship who lives in Los Angeles and Berlin.

title: Mario Adorf
description: Mario Adorf, born in 1930 in Zurich, Switzerland, is a German actor famous for playing villains. Among other awards, he received the "Pardo alla Carriera" for his life's work at the Locarno Film Festival.

title: Edinburgh Festival Fringe
description: The Edinburgh Festival Fringe, founded in 1947, is the world's largest arts festival and focuses on theater and comedy. It takes place every year in the Scottish capital in August.

title: Hieronymus Bosch
description: Hieronymus Bosch (1450-1516) was one of the most significant early Dutch painters from the late medieval period. He is particularly renowned for his mysterious depictions of religious themes, including hell.

title: Audrey Tautou
description: Audrey Tautou, born in Beaumont, France, in 1976, is a successful French actress. She is best known for her leading role in the 2001 film "Amélie."

title: Search engine
description: A search engine is a program designed to look for information stored on a computer or a network like the internet.

title: Robert Redford
description: Robert Redford was a successful Hollywood actor, director and producer who founded the Sundance Film Festival. He was also a passionate environmentalist, founding the Institute for Resource Management mediation group.

title: German Book Prize
description: The German Book Prize, created in 2005, honors the year's best German-language novel published in Germany, Austria or Switzerland.

title: #DailyDrone

description: Coronaviruses are found in humans and other animals. Different strains cause illnesses of varying severity — from the common cold to SARS to COVID-19. The pandemic declared in March 2020 was caused by a coronavirus.

title: US election 2020
description: The US election ended with former-Vice President Joe Biden winning the presidency over Republican incumbent Donald Trump. In the midst of a pandemic and with the economy reeling, the campaign was long and contentious.

title: How do we change?
description: The Corona pandemic has changed the world. But if we are capable of such sweeping change, what does this mean for our species as we face the future of our sweltering planet? And more importantly: How do we change?

title: #DailyDrone - UNESCO World Heritage
description: The #DailyDrone shows you all 46 UNESCO natural and cultural Heritage Sites in Germany.

title: Internet Freedom
description: The internet has become a global tool for freedom of expression. But millions of people are denied access to the internet through censorship, shutdowns and state entities seeking to dictate what people see and do online.

title: Kamala Harris
description: Kamala Harris was the vice president of the United States from 2021 to 2025, under President Joe Biden. She was the Democratic Party candidate for the 2024 US presidential election, losing to Republican Donald Trump.

title: Coronavirus vaccine
description: There are hundreds of potential coronavirus vaccines under development worldwide. We're following their progress from research to development to approval, launch and application.

title: Fact check
description: Viral fake news on social media, false claims on COVID-19 or disinformation on elections — DW's Fact check team debunks, explains and uses in-depth research techniques to separate fact from fiction.

title: Abdel Fattah el-Sissi
description: Abdel Fattah el-Sissi took office as the sixth president of Egypt in June 2014 after a 2013 military coup that deposed former President Mohamed Morsi.

title: Black Lives Matter movement
description: Black Lives Matter is a decentralized social movement founded in the US in 2013. It aims to protest at racially motivated violence against Black people.

title: German election 2021
description: Some 60.4 million people are eligible to vote in Germany's general election for the lower house of parliament, the Bundestag, on September 26, 2021.

title: Annalena Baerbock
description: Annalena Baerbock is the President of the UN General Assembly. She was Germany's foreign minister from 2021 to 2025.

title: Markus Söder
description: Markus Söder is a Bavarian politician. He is Bavaria’s state premier and head of the Christian Social Union (CSU), the conservative Bavarian allies to the Christian Democratic Union (CDU).

title: Olaf Scholz
description: Olaf Scholz is a German politician from the Social Democratic Party. He was elected chancellor in 2021. He previously served as federal minister of finance and vice-chancellor under Angela Merkel from 2018 to 2021.

title: 1,700 years of Jewish life in Germany
description: Germany celebrated the diversity of Jewish life in the anniversary year of 2021. Jewish-German history dates back 1,700 years and began with a Roman decree in 321 CE.

title: Israel-Hamas conflict in Gaza
description: On October 7, 2023, the militant group Hamas led terrorist attacks against Israel, which responded by launching a war in Gaza. A fragile ceasefire began in October 2025, but the humanitarian situation remains dire.

title: Merkel’s Era: The Women of Power
description: In our series "Merkel’s Era: The Women of Power" we talk to powerful women in the world of politics.

title: Floods in Germany
description: The southern states of Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg have been inundated, causing dam bursts and prompting dramatic rescues. States of emergency have been declared in several areas with more heavy rain expected.

title: Global Ideas
description: We focus on "best practice" climate and biodiversity protection projects that offer solutions. Global Ideas is supported by the German environment ministry within the framework of its International Climate Initiative.

title: Coalition talks in Germany
description: Following the September 26, 2021 elections, Germany's three main parties started holding exploratory talks. On November 25, they presented an agreement.
