title: Pandora Papers
description: A trove of leaked documents, known as the Pandora Papers, has revealed links between current and former world leaders and their secret offshore tax havens.

title: COP27: Everything you need to know
description: The international community came together for the COP27 UN Climate Change Conference in Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt, seeking solutions to humanity's biggest threat.

title: Friedrich Merz
description: Friedrich Merz is the 10th chancellor of the Federal Republic of Germany. He is also the chairman of Germany's center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU).

title: Alice Weidel
description: Alice Elisabeth Weidel is a German politician, Bundestag lawmaker and the co-leader of the far-right populist Alternative for Germany (AfD).

title: Robert Habeck
description: Robert Habeck is Green Party politician who became economy and energy minister, and vice-chancellor in an SPD-led coalition governing Germany in 2021.

title: Tino Chrupalla
description: Tino Chrupalla took over as one of the co-chairs of the far-right populist Alternative for Germany (AfD) in 2019.

title: United Kingdom
description: The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, mostly known as the United Kingdom (UK) or Britain, is a nation in northwestern Europe.

title: Russia's war in Ukraine
description: Russia launched a full-scale war on Ukraine in February 2022, an escalation of a conflict that began with Russia's annexation of Crimea in 2014.

title: Walter Lübcke
description: Walter Lübcke was a center-right politician from the Christian Democrat Party (CDU). He was killed on June 2, 2019 by a far-right extremist.

title: Germany national football team
description: There has been much soul-searching since Germany exited the World Cup. Germany had long been one of the world's most successful footballing nations. The men have won four World Cups, second only to Brazil's five.

title: Law and Justice
description: Here you can find a compilation of DW content related to law and justice.

title: China-Taiwan crisis
description: Differences over Taiwan's status have flared tensions between China and Taiwan. China sees the island, which is governed independently, as a breakaway province.

title: Demographics
description: Demographic data show factors such as age, race and gender in a society.

title: Labor issues
description: Labor and related issues pertain to all aspects of the supply of and demand for labor in any given country. They also encompass labor disputes and strikes over wages, benefits and working hours.

title: Rhine River
description: The Rhine is Germany's longest river. It has been an important transportation link between the north and south of Europe for thousands of years.

title: Beethovenfest
description: Every September, the city of Bonn honors its son Ludwig van Beethoven with a four-week music festival. The festival was first held on a small scale in 1845, and today the program features around 60 performances.

title: Uyghur community
description: The Uyghur, a Turkic-speaking minority based in China's northwestern Xinjiang province, view Beijing as a "colonizing power" attempting to undermine their political rights.

title: J.R.R. Tolkien
description: John Ronald Reuel Tolkien (1892 – 1973) was a British poet, academic and writer best known for his fantasy sagas "The Hobbit" and "The Lord of the Rings."

title: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
description: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (1749-1832), Germany's most renowned poet, was also known for his plays, literature and aesthetic criticism as well as treatises on botany, anatomy and color.

title: Soviet Union
description: The Soviet Union was a transcontinental state comprising of 15 republics that spanned much of Eurasia from 1922 to 1991.

title: Energy crisis
description: An energy crisis is a critical bottleneck in the supply of energy. When fuel prices rise it's usually bad news for the economy, but it also offers the opportunity to transition to clean and renewable energy sources.

title: Russia's partial mobilization
description: Facing setbacks in Ukraine, Russian President Vladimir Putin has ordered a partial mobilization of hundreds of thousands of army reservists. The move has sparked protests across Russia, with many fleeing conscription.

title: Giorgia Meloni
description: Giorgia Meloni is Italy's first female prime minister at the head of the country's most right-wing government since World War II.

title: UN Security Council
description: The Security Council is one of the six principal organs of the United Nations and is charged with ensuring peace and security. China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States are permanent members.

title: Nord Stream pipelines
description: Nord Stream, a pair of natural gas pipelines running through the Baltic Sea, was a key factor in securing Europe's energy security before war broke out in Ukraine. It was damaged in an undersea explosion in Sept. 2022.

title: Right Livelihood Award
description: The Right Livelihood Award, also known as the Alternative Nobel, is awarded annually to honor and support courageous people solving global problems.

title: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva
description: Leftist Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva — more commonly known as Lula — was elected for the first time in 2002 and served as Brazil's president for two terms until 2010. He won the presidency again in January 2023.

title: Nobel Prize
description: The Nobel Prize is an annual award for outstanding achievements. Each day in early October, selection committees announce the yearly laureates in one of six categories. The award ceremony is in December.

title: DW Festival Concert
description: In this audio show, Cristina Burack takes you through the best concerts from classical music festivals in Germany.

title: South Korea
description: South Korea is a country in east Asia on the southern portion of the Korean peninsula. It has a population of over 51 million and is a major player in global trade, particularly in the technology and automotive sectors.

title: Mental health
description: Mental health refers to our emotional, psychological, and social well-being. Mental health issues might emerge as hereditary disorders or conditions caused by traumatic events or damaged interpersonal connections.

title: Liquefied natural gas (LNG)
description: Compared with natural gas, liquefied natural gas is easier to ship and store. But the energy required to liquefy, ship, store and convert the fossil fuel back into a gas makes it more destructive for the environment.

title: Nuclear weapons
description: Nuclear bombs are one of the deadliest weapons of mass destruction. To date, the only use of nuclear weapons in armed conflict occurred in 1945 when the United States dropped bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in Japan.

title: Jina Mahsa Amini
description: Jina Mahsa Amini, a 22-year-old Kurdish Iranian woman, died in police custody in September 2022, accused of improperly wearing a hijab. Her death sparked months of protest, largely led by women and schoolgirls.

title: 2022 Iran protests
description: The death of 22-year-old Kurdish woman Jina Mahsa Amini in Sept. 2022 sparked demonstrations and violent crackdowns on the streets of Iran. Largely led by women and schoolgirls, the protests call for political change.

title: Eco India — The Environment Magazine
description: Eco India, a show dedicated to the amazing Indian subcontinent. Weekly episodes feature compelling stories from Asia and Europe on the environment, sustainability, technology and social issues.

title: Poverty in Germany
description: Germany has struggled to cope with the impact of the Russian invasion of Ukraine, which sent prices for energy and food soaring.

title: Global Us – The Globalization Program
description: There are eight billion people on Earth and we are better connected than ever before. How can we make use of that? From Global 3000 comes Global Us – because we need joint action now more than ever.

title: Eco Africa — The Environment Magazine
description: DW's Eco Africa showcases innovative concepts and best practice projects from Africa and Europe and presents environment and climate change ideas that inspire others to get on board or start something of their own.

title: Cost-of-living crisis
description: Soaring prices for food and energy, triggered by conflict and widespread labor shortages, are affecting people across the globe.

title: Sudan crisis
description: The third Sudanese civil war began on April 15, 2023, between the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces and Sudan's military. Resulting violence and famine have displaced some 14 million and killed hundreds of thousands.

title: US midterm elections 2022
description: Held in the middle of a presidential term, midterm elections are usually regarded as a referendum on the sitting president's policies. Voters choose all member of the House of Representatives and a third of the Senate.

title: Goncourt Prize
description: The Prix Goncourt is considered France's oldest and most pregious literary prize and is awarded annually in November for the best work of fiction.

title: Psychology
description: Psychologists study the brain and behavior. Psychology is a relatively young scientific field, but it’s fascinated scientists for as long as physiology. The two are totally intertwined and central to a healthy life.

title: Anita Lasker-Wallfisch
description: Anita Lasker-Wallfisch is a German-British cellist. A Jew deported to Auschwitz, she survived the Holocaust by playing the cello in the Birkenau concentration camp orchestra.

title: Remote work
description: When employees do their jobs from a location other than an employer's central office. Remote workers are sometimes called digital nomads.

title: Tackling Africa's climate change challenges
description: Africa emits the least greenhouse gases, yet the continent is the most vulnerable to the impacts of climate change.

title: Jamal Khashoggi
description: Saudi journalist Jamal Khashoggi was murdered on October 2, 2018 at the Saudi consulate in Istanbul. Five of the alleged killers were convicted in 2020, but the Saudi crown prince has also been accused of involvement.

title: German politics
description: What's making news in Germany? From Bundestag debates to political controversy and pressing social issues, we bring you the stories and the people behind the headlines.

title: Thanksgiving
description: A holiday celebrated primarily in the United States which takes place on the fourth Thursday of each November. It celebrates a shared dinner in 1621 between English colonists known as Pilgrims and the Wampanoag people.

title: Living with disability in Africa
description: December 3 is the International Day for Persons with Disabilities. Disabled people in Africa often cannot get an education or even a job to survive.

title: Violence against women
description: Violence against women and girls is one of the most prevalent human rights violations. It includes acts that cause physical, sexual or emotional harm or suffering as well as the threat of harm.

title: Ingrid Bergman
description: Ingrid Bergman (1915-1982) was an award-winning Swedish-born actress. She is often described as one of the most influential stars in film history.

title: Humphrey Bogart
description: Humphrey Bogart (1899-1957) was a US film and stage actor. His most significant romantic lead role was in the iconic drama "Casablanca" (1942).

title: Hans Magnus Enzensberger
description: Writer, cultural critic, translator and publisher: Hans Magnus Enzensberger (1929-2022) was one of Germany's leading intellectuals.

title: Christmas market
description: Locals and tourists come to sip mulled wine, eat food and purchase hand-made Christmas presents at Europe's Christmas markets, which are especially popular in Germany. Each year, around 3,000 markets are held in Germany.

title: Immigration and German citizenship
description: Germany wants to revamp its immigration system and citizenship laws to make it easier for foreign skilled workers to come to the country and fill job vacancies that are at a record high.

title: Meghan, Duchess of Sussex
description: Meghan Markle is a former US actress and the wife of Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex.

title: DW Freedom
description: DW Freedom: The Media Development Think Tank. Insights, analysis and a global exchange of ideas on freedom of expression, digital technology and the media.

title: Climate protests
description: Activists are finding new ways to draw attention to the devastating effects of climate change. In Germany, and the rest of Europe, discussion about whether such protests are criminal or not has been heating up.

title: Cryptocurrency
description: A cryptocurrency is a digital or virtual currency that uses cryptography, the process of encoding and decoding data, to secure transactions. Buying and selling is done using a blockchain, a decentralized public ledger.

title: Benin Bronzes
description: A large group of sculptures from the former Kingdom of Benin (modern-day Nigeria) that were stolen from British colonialists in 1897. They are at the center of a restitution process throughout Europe.

title: Cyril Ramaphosa
description: Cyril Ramaphosa became South Africa's president in 2018, following the resignation of the scandal-ridden Jacob Zuma. He currently stands at the helm of the ruling African National Congress party, the ANC.

title: German health system
description: The health care system in Germany is organized partly at the state level and partly at the private level. The structure is strongly influenced by the country's federalist system.

title: Wagner Group
description: The Wagner Group is a private Russian mercenary unit fighting in Ukraine and elsewhere. Its former leader, Yevgeny Prigozhin, was presumed dead after a 2023 plane crash. Since 2024, it is also known as Africa Corps.

title: Pope Benedict XVI
description: Cardinal Joseph Ratzinger was elected head of the Catholic Church in 2005, and was Pope Benedict XVI until he retired in 2013. He stayed true to his conservative path throughout his papacy. He died on December 31, 2022.

title: Social media ban legislation
description: Pressure is growing to hold social media platforms to account for data privacy and disinformation. The impact of app usage on mental health and the polarization of public discourse have also come under scrutiny.

title: European Capital of Culture
description: The title "European Capital of Culture" is awarded by the European Union. The goal is to showcase the diversity of Europe's heritage and strengthen citizens' identification with Europe

title: Movement of Democratic Forces of Casamance (MFDC)
description: The MFDC is a rebel group which has waged a low-intensity campaign for independence for the southern Senegalese region of Casamance, which lies on the border with Gambia.

title: March 23 (M23) Movement
description: The M23 rebel group in the Democratic Republic of Congo reemerged from dormancy in 2022 and has since advanced across the country's troubled North Kivu province, sending hundreds of thousands of people fleeing in fear.

title: Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF)
description: The TPLF was founded in the 1970s by a small group of left-wing nationalist militiamen. They vowed to fight for the rights of Tigrayans, a relatively small ethnic group that account for just 5% of Ethiopia's population.

title: Rare earth elements
description: Rare earth minerals are a group of elements crucial for electronics, defense and auto industries as well as other high-tech products.

title: Antibiotics
description: Antibiotics prevent and treat certain types of bacterial infection. During the world week of antimicrobial resistance awareness, something experts call a growing global health crisis, antibiotics are an important focus.

title: China economy
description: China's economy, the world's second-largest, is a socialist market economy that has made great strides over the past decades. However, it is currently struggling with deflation in its consumer sector and sluggish growth.

title: Climate activism
description: From local grassroots strategies to nationwide campaigns, climate activists — many of them young people — are demanding that governments and industry step up the fight against climate change.

title: Franco-German relations
description: More than 60 years since the signing of the Elysee Treaty, there's mounting pressure for France and Germany to revamp their cooperation and leadership within the EU.

title: Burkina Faso
description: Burkina Faso is a landlocked state and one of the poorest and most volatile in Africa. The country is reeling from jihadist violence that swept in from neighboring Mali in 2015.

title: Silicon Valley
description: The world's preeminent hub for technology, Silicon Valley is a byword for innovation. It is home to many of the world's largest high-tech corporations as well as thousands of promising startups.

title: US economy
description: The US economy is the world's largest by nominal GDP. Its firms are at or near the forefront in technological advances and the US dollar the currency most used in global transactions and the foremost reserve currency.

title: Inflation Reduction Act
description: The Inflation Reduction Act is a landmark US law which aims to curb inflation by reducing the deficit, lowering prescription drug prices, and investing into domestic energy production while promoting clean energy.

title: Notre Dame
description: The UNESCO World Heritage Site, built on the Seine island in the heart of Paris, was partially destroyed in a 2019 fire. The iconic medieval cathedral reopened in December 2024 after five years of speedy reconstruction.

title: Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen
description: Born in March 1845, Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen discovered X-rays, which are used in medicine and elsewhere to produce images of internal organs. Röntgen received the 1901 Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in February 1923.

title: Satellites
description: We think of satellites as spacecraft, collecting Earth observation data or connecting us via the internet. But, in fact, anything that orbits a planet or star is a satellite, including moons, planets, and machines.

title: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs)
description: The World Health Organization says there are more than 30 known sexually transmitted infections (STIs). They include bacteria, viruses and parasites that can be transmitted via vaginal, anal and oral sex.

title: Medical marijuana
description: Possession of and smoking cannabis for recreational use remains illegal in many places, but some countries, including the USA and Uruguay, are legalizing its use in medicine to treat conditions, such as chronic pain.

title: Earthquakes
description: There are about 500,000 detectable earthquakes every year — 90% are in the Pacific Ring of Fire. But the most seismic region is the Alpide belt, which runs east from the Mediterranean to Turkey, Iran and northern India.

title: Sexuality education
description: The World Health Organization says sexuality — or sex — education is about teaching young people responsible sexual behavior, and that research in Europe shows young people do not get sexually active earlier as a result.

title: Nigeria 2023 Election
description: More than 93 million Nigerians were eligible to vote on February 25. The election occurred at a moment of a national cash crisis and widespread insecurity, and with the proliferation of fake news and disinformation.

title: Water scarcity
description: The world's freshwater resources are limited and increasingly at risk. At the same time, rivers, lakes and groundwater are increasingly affected by pollution and climate change

title: Semiconductor industry
description: Semiconductors, also referred to as microchips, are components typically found in computers, mobile phones, cars and artificial intelligence. They use raw materials like Silicon, Germanium and metals.

title: Turkey elections
description: On May 28, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan secured yet another term in office, after an historic runoff election. The incumbent was challenged by opposition candidate Kemal Kilicdaroglu.

title: Overweight and obesity
description: Overweight and obesity constitute a major global public health crisis, affecting almost 3 billion people worldwide.

title: Human spaceflight
description: With the launch of Artemis II, NASA has sent the first manned mission to fly past the moon since Apollo 17 in 1972.

title: Silicon Valley Bank
description: A US bank that mainly catered to tech startups in Silicon Valley has failed, sending shock waves across the startup community and financial markets worldwide. The collapse has sparked fears of global contagion risks.

title: LGBTQ+ rights in Africa
description: The rights of LGBTQ+ people are limited by draconian laws across much of the African continent, with homosexuality outlawed in dozens of countries.

title: Bangladesh
description: Bangladesh is in a state of political turmoil after weeks of student-led mass protests, which drew the curtain on PM Sheikh Hasina's 15-year rule. Elections for a new government took place on February 12.

title: Nuclear energy
description: Germany has shut down its last three nuclear reactors. But elsewhere around the globe, nuclear energy is making a comeback.

title: Volodymyr Zelenskyy
description: Volodymyr Zelenskyy was elected president in 2019 and has led Ukraine since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion. First seen as a political lightweight, the former comedian has rallied support at home and abroad.

title: Rising sea levels
description: As higher temperatures cause ice sheets to melt, sea levels are — rising leaving coastal communities around the world to look for solutions. Some are opting to relocate, while others build defenses to keep the ocean out.

title: China's Belt and Road Initiative
description: China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI), also referred to as the New Silk Road, is a massive infrastructure project launched in 2013 by President Xi Jinping to boost China's economic and political influence.

title: US election 2024
description: Republican Donald Trump was elected the 47th president of the United States in the November 5 election, defeating Kamala Harris of the Democrats.

title: Right-wing extremism
description: From neo-Nazis in Europe to white supremacist movements in the United States to religious nationalists in Latin America and beyond, right-wing extremism is a consistent — and growing — threat to cultures and societies.

title: Narendra Modi
description: Narendra Modi is the prime minister of India who has won two national elections. He has been credited with positioning the country as a leading power, but his party has been criticized for its Hindu nationalist agenda.

title: EU migration policy
description: Despite the EU's new migration and asylum policy, people are still dying as they try to reach the bloc. The trip across the Mediterranean Sea to Europe is the deadliest migratory route in the world.

title: Military science in China
description: German universities attract many international academics and engineers. DW investigations suggest some return home to China where they work for the military.

title: Germany's skilled workers shortage
description: As a severe labor shortage bites, Germany looks to reform its immigration laws.

title: Sportswashing
description: Sportswashing aims to blur the line between sports, politics, and propaganda, raising questions about the genuine motives behind the funding of sports events or clubs.

title: Germany's domestic intelligence agency
description: Germany's Bundesamt für Verfassungsschutz (BfV), or Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution, monitors political extremists with a view to preventing terrorist attacks.

title: Titanic sub
description: All five passengers aboard the Titan submersible are believed dead, after the US Coast Guard said it had recovered pieces of debris from the missing vessel.

title: Jamshid Sharmahd
description: Jamshid Sharmahd is an Iranian-German software engineer. In 2022 he received the death penalty for alleged involvement in a 2008 attack on a mosque in Shiraz that killed 14 people and injured 200.

title: Yevgeny Prigozhin
description: Yevgeny Prigozhin founded the Wagner group, a private militia that fought some of the deadliest battles in Russia's invasion of Ukraine. In August 2023, he was killed in a plane crash in Russia.

title: Rishi Sunak
description: Rishi Sunak is the current UK prime minister and Conservative Party leader. After holding Cabinet positions under Boris Johnson, he succeeded Liz Truss to become the first British Asian prime minister in October 2022.

title: European Court of Human Rights (ECHR)
description: The ECHR is the international court of the Council of Europe (not the EU). It has sitting judges from each of the 46 member states of the Council and enforces the European Convention on Human Rights.

title: Far-right populism in Europe
description: Far-right populist movements have steadily built support across Europe in recent years, opposing immigration, minority rights and measures to tackle climate change.

title: Marina Abramovic
description: Serbian performance artist Marina Abramovic is known for her work involving extreme physical experiences. She has combed her scalp bloody, laid down on blocks of ice or run into concrete pillars.

title: Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant
description: The Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant is the largest in Europe, and supplies one fifth of Ukraine's energy. Russian troops took control of it shortly after Moscow's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

title: Boris Pistorius
description: Boris Pistorius has been serving as Germany's Defense Minister since January 2023.

title: El Salvador
description: El Salvador is a small country in Central America. It suffered a civil war from 1979-1992. Attempts to diservify its economy from mining and coffee included 2022 legislation to make Bitcoin legal tender in the country.

title: South Sudan
description: South Sudan gained independence on July 9, 2011, after seceding from Sudan, its neighbor to the north. Since then, the oil-rich nation has seen years of civil upheaval, which has impeded social and economic advancement.

title: Bettina Stark-Watzinger
description: Germany's Federal Education Minister is a trained econimist and served as a lawmaker for the neoliberal Free Democrats (FDP) from 2018.

title: Nancy Faeser
description: Nancy Faeser is a German lawyer and politician of the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) and has served as Federal Minister of the Interior since 2021.

title: Germany-China relations
description: China is Germany's biggest trading partner. But geopolitical concerns have led to a more strained relationship.

title: Sahel region
description: The Sahel is a vast region between the Sahara and the Sudanian savanna in Africa. The area faces environmental issues linked to climate change, and is a base for many terrorist groups in Northern Africa.

title: Foreign direct investment
description: FDI is when an investor residing in one country takes a direct stake in an enterprise or project in another. It can take several forms, including M&As, investment of funds, or the construction of new facilities.

title: Neurotransmitters
description: Neurotransmitters are tiny messengers that pass information from one neuron to another. Neurons are basic cells of the nervous system, without which we couldn't function — use our senses, think, speak, or move our limbs.

title: Embryonic research
description: Scientists say research with embryos can help us understand the causes of miscarriages, genetic conditions and congenital organ defects. But the research is controversial and banned in many places.

title: Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)
description: The 15-member Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) is a regional political and economic bloc. The group is facing an existential crisis after Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger announced their intention to leave.

title: Breastfeeding
description: The World Health Organization says breastfeeding is one of the most effective ways to ensure a child’s health: Breastmilk is safe, clean and contains antibodies that help protect against many common childhood illnesses.

title: The Flip Side: A different angle on Africa's big stories
description: Short videos exposing the hidden angles of Africa's trending topics. Welcome to the Flip Side! We turn reporting about the continent on its head.

title: James Webb Space Telescope (JWST)
description: The JWST detects light in the infrared range, allowing astronomers to see through clouds of dust and gas in space, right back in time to the formation of the first stars and galaxies, more than 13.5 billion years ago.

title: Anwar Ibrahim
description: Anwar Ibrahim has served as prime minister of Malaysia since November 2022. He served in successive governments since the 1980s and was jailed in 1999 after a trial for sodomy and corruption, criticized by rights groups

title: The Yazidi
description: The ethno-religious Yazidi community mostly resides in northern Iraq. In 2014, the minority, thought to number around 500,000 inside Iraq, became a target for the extremist group known as the "Islamic State."

title: Venice Film Festival
description: One of the three major European film festivals alongside Cannes and Berlin, the annual event in Italy is the world's oldest of its kind and renowned for its selection of films of high artistic quality.

title: Morocco earthquake
description: Thousands of people were killed or injured in Morocco after a 6.8 magnitude earthquake southwest of Marrakech on September 8.

title: Law and Justice (PiS)
description: Law and Justice (Prawo I Sprawiedliwosc, PiS for short) is a Polish populist, conservative political party founded in 2001. Currently in opposition, it remains one of Poland's most popular parties.

title: Sustainable Development Goals
description: The United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals, or SDGs, are 17 goals that all member states have agreed to try to achieve by 2030.

title: Nagorno-Karabakh
description: The Nagorno-Karabakh conflict is a long-running ethnic and territorial dispute between Armenia and Azerbaijan, in the South Caucasus region between Europe and Asia.

title: Free Voters
description: The "Freie Wähler" Free Voters are a conservative, populist political party in Germany's southern state of Bavaria.

title: Hindu nationalism
description: Hindu nationalism has been on the rise in India since Narendra Modi came to power in 2014. The ideology is based mainly on the supremacy of Hinduism, with religious minorities in India complaining of persecution.

title: Autoimmune disease
description: In autoimmune diseases, the immune system malfunctions and attacks healthy cells, tissues and organs. There are more than 80 autoimmune diseases, including multiple sclerosis, Type I diabetes and celiac disease.

title: Immune system
description: The human immune system protects our bodies against germs, including bacteria, viruses, fungi and toxins. It's a complex network of organs, cells and proteins that us live healthy lives.

title: European Political Community (EPC)
description: The European Political Community was founded in Prague on October 6, 2022 in response to Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. It brings together leaders from 44 European countries, including non-EU members.

title: COP28: Everything you need to know
description: The COP28 UN Climate Change Conference in Dubai sought solutions to climate change, humanity's biggest threat.

title: South China Sea conflict
description: Conflicting territorial claims in the South China Sea have created a web of rivalries and acrimony between China, Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines and Vietnam.

title: November Pogroms of 1938
description: On November 9, 1938, Nazis and civilians who supported them destroyed Jewish-owned shops and synagogues in Germany, Austria and the Sudetenland. The pogroms were a new step in systematic efforts to eradicate Jews.

title: United Arab Emirates
description: The United Arab Emirates, or UAE, comprises seven different emirates ruled by different royal families, with Abu Dhabi acting as the capital. The UAE is among the world's 10 largest oil producers.

title: Loss and damage through climate change
description: Rising temperatures are leading to increasingly extreme weather events, most impacting countries that have contributed least to warming. They have long called for a designated fund to compensate for loss and damage.

title: Non-fungible token (NFT)
description: NFTs are assets that are represented by a non-fungible token, a unique digital identifier that cannot be copied and is recorded in a blockchain for security and transparency.

title: African digital natives
description: Young Africans protect themselves against scammers, Internet stalkers, digital addiction and more in this exciting digital literacy series.

title: Germany's Basic Law
description: The Basic Law is the Federal Republic of Germany's constitution, which came into effect in May 1949.

title: Wolfgang Schäuble
description: Wolfgang Schäuble, a member of the Christian Democrats, was one of Germany's most influential politicians. His roles included minister of interior, finance minister and, finally, president of the German parliament.

title: Björn Höcke
description: Björn Höcke is a German far-right extremist politician with the Alternative for Germany party (AfD) in the eastern state of Thuringia. In his statements and writings, he uses fascist, antisemitic and racist language.

title: Islamophobia
description: Islamophobia reflects a deep fear of and hostility toward Islam and Muslims and their politics and culture. It can result in hate speech and hate crimes against Muslims and their way of life.

title: Franz Beckenbauer
description: Franz Beckenbauer was one of the greatest names in world football. The German legend won all there is to win both as a player and a coach, but his legacy was also tarnished by corruption allegations.

title: German agriculture
description: Farming only generates just under 1% of Germany's GDP — less than in France, to the west, and Poland, to the east. Germany receives €6 billion per year in EU farming subsidies.

title: Sahra Wagenknecht
description: Sahra Wagenknecht was born in 1969 in Jena, East Germany, to a German mother and Iranian father. She has founded a party combining conservative social values with socialist economic values.

title: EU elections 2024
description: People in the EU's 27 member states went to the polls in early June to vote for a new European Parliament. The outcome will also shape the European Commission for the next five years.

title: Illegal drug trade
description: The illegal drug trade involves the cultivation, distribution and sale of substances that violate drug prohibition laws. The trade can fuel corruption, money laundering and human exploitation.

title: Climate change solutions
description: Greenhouse gas emissions from burning fossil fuels, agriculture and deforestation are causing the world's climate to change, threatening people, plants and animals. But humanity has solutions to stop planetary heating.

title: Mozambique
description: Police have clamped down on protests following Mozambique's presidential election. The opposition is calling attention to irregularities ahead of the release of results — which are expected to favor the ruling party.

title: Cote d'Ivoire
description: Cote d'Ivoire, also known as Ivory Coast, is a presidential republic in West Africa with a population of about 32 million. It borders Burkina Faso, Ghana, Guinea, Liberia, Mali and the Atlantic Ocean.

title: Energy communities
description: Energy communities are collective, citizen-driven initiatives that seek to generate and share sustainable energy at community level. They often take the form of collectives and contribute to the clean energy transition.

title: Trade unions
description: Trade unions are witnessing a resurgence in many countries as workers hit with a cost-of-living crisis demand better pay and working conditions. Here is a compilation of DW's reporting on trade unions.

title: Sierra Leone
description: Sierra Leone was a key departure point for thousands of African captives during the transatlantic slave trade. The West African nation has made steady progress since the 1991-2002 civil war and the 2014 Ebola outbreak.

title: Cem Özdemir
description: Cem Özdemir is a German politician is a member of the Green Party and is the head of government in the southwestern state of Baden-Württemberg.

title: Cape Verde
description: Cape Verde is a tiny African archipelago of 10 islands in the Atlantic Ocean about 600 kilometers (373 miles) away from Senegal on Africa's western coast. It gained independence from Portugal on July 5, 1975.

title: Central African Republic
description: The Central African Republic (CAR) is a landlocked nation in the center of the African continent that borders Cameroon, Chad, Congo, Republic of Congo, South Sudan and Sudan.

title: Madagascar
description: Madagascar is an East African island nation located in the Indian Ocean, east of Mozambique. The former French colony is the leading global producer of vanilla but also one of the world's poorest countries.

title: Guinea-Bissau
description: Guinea-Bissau is a West African country with a population of 2 million that borders the Atlantic Ocean, Guinea and Senegal. Guinea-Bissau gained independence in 1974 after a bloody war against Portugal.

title: Transnistria
description: Transnistria is a separatist region in the east of the Republic of Moldova. It broke away from the former Soviet republic of Moldova in 1990, but is not recognized by any country in the world.

title: Alliance for Social Justice and Economic Reason (BSW)
description: The BSW, formerly known as Bündnis Sahra Wagenknecht (Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance), was founded in 2024 and combines left-leaning economic and conservative migration policy initiatives.

title: Equatorial Guinea
description: Equatorial Guinea is a Central African nation that is considered one of Africa's richest due to its huge mineral and oil reserves. It's the only African country to have Spanish as an official language.

title: Mauritania
description: Mauritania is a sparsely populated nation of 4 million people that borders Algeria, Mali, Morocco and Senegal in Western Africa's Sahel region. It achieved independence from France in 1960.

title: Seychelles
description: Seychelles is an Indian Ocean archipelago with a population of around 100,000, making it the least populated nation in Africa. Seychelles is a major tourist destination that's famous for its idyllic white beaches.

title: Sao Tome and Principe
description: Sao Tome and Principe is an African island nation located to the west of Gabon. It's the second-smallest African country after Seychelles. Sao Tome and Principe gained independence from Portugal in 1975.

title: Republic of the Congo
description: The Republic of the Congo is a central African nation whose capital is Brazzaville. It borders Angola, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Congo and Gabon. The Republic of Congo gained independence from France in 1960.

title: Baltimore bridge collapse
description: A container ship hit a support of the Francis Scott Key Bridge causing the structure to collapse. Six people working on the bridge were presumed dead. It is unclear what caused a power outage on the vessel.

title: Rwanda: 30 years since genocide
description: More than 1 million people — mostly from the Tutsi minority ethnic group — were systematically murdered by Hutu extremists during a 100-day killing spree that started on April 7, 1994.

title: Fast fashion
description: Fast fashion has become a massive trend in the textile industry, disrupting how clothing is made and marketed. Explore its impact in this selection of recent DW content on the topic.

title: India elections 2024
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's BJP won the most seats following in the election, which ran from April 19 to June 1. Though Modi will hold a third consecutive term in office, the party's wins were smaller than projected.

title: Weimar Republic
description: The Weimar Republic refers to the phase of the first parliamentary democracy in Germany from 1918 to 1933, which ended when the National Socialists seized power.

title: DW Freedom of Speech Award
description: Each year, DW honors an individual or initiative promoting freedom of expression and human rights with the Freedom of Speech Award. This year, the honor goes to Hong Kong media mogul Jimmy Lai.

title: Tuberculosis
description: Tuberculosis (TB) is a bacterial infection that affects the lungs. It spreads through the air via coughs, sneezes and saliva. With annual infection rates about 10 million, health experts say we face a 'TB epidemic'.

title: CRISPR-cas9 (human gene therapy)
description: Human gene therapy is a method of modifying a person's genes to treat or cure disease. Gene therapies can replace or inactivate a disease-causing gene with a healthy copy of the same gene.

title: Jewish life in Europe
description: Jewish life is an integral part of Europe's past and present. How do Jewish Europeans live, keep their traditions and customs alive and view both current developments and the way the past is dealt with?

title: AI Lexicon
description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is everywhere. Do you know your AI from your ML? Aside from DW's general coverage, we're compiling a living lexicon with easy-to-understand definitions and examples of AI in everyday life.

title: Robert Fico
description: Robert Fico is currently serving his fourth term as Slovakia's prime minister. The leftist-populist politician was shot and wounded during an assassination attempt in a small Slovak town in May 2024.

title: Dominican Republic
description: The Dominican Republic is a Caribbean country that shares the island of Hispaniola with Haiti to its west. It has a population of roughly 11.5 million and is comparatively wealthy by its neighbors' standards.

title: Ebrahim Raisi
description: Ebrahim Raisi was elected president of Iran in 2021. The hard-liner, who previously headed the country's judiciary, was known for his connections to Iran's religious leaders, including Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

title: South Africa election 2024
description: The African National Congress (ANC), which liberated the country from apartheid in 1994, lost its 30-year majority in the May 29 vote. Follow DW for what might be coming next as South Africa enters uncharted territory.

title: Yulia Navalnaya
description: A leading figure in the Russian opposition, Yulia Navalnaya has vowed to continue the work of her late husband, Kremlin critic Alexei Navalny. Living in exile, she was honored with DW's Freedom of Speech Award in 2024.

title: Global South
description: The Global South refers to states often described as "developing nations," mostly located in the Southern Hemisphere. By 2030, the Global South will likely include two of the world's largest economies, China and India.

title: Freedom of speech
description: Freedom of speech, or freedom of expression, is the right of an individual or a group to express their opinions without the fear of reprisals, censorship or legal repercussions.

title: Genetics and genomics
description: Both genetics and genomics are important for our understanding of health and disease. While genetics is the study of individual genes, genomics is the study of the entire set of a person's genes — their genome.

title: DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid)
description: It's said that DNA makes us who and what we are. More specifically, DNA is a sequence of genes which provides instructions, or code, that allow us to produce proteins, which are essential to the way we function and live.

title: State elections in Saxony, Thuringia and Brandenburg
description: Germany is paying close attention to results of two state elections in eastern Germany ahead of a nationwide vote set for 2025. The far-right populist AfD made gains in Saxony and Thuringia.

title: Health care in Germany
description: Germany's health care system is creaking as medical professionals are insufficient for an aging population.

title: Ursula von der Leyen
description: Ursula von der Leyen, a German politician and a member of the conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU), has been serving as the president of the European Commission since 2019.

title: COP29 Azerbaijan
description: Finance and a transition from fossil fuels topped the agenda at the UN's COP29 climate conference, which took place in Azerbaijan's capital, Baku, from November 11-22.

title: Southern African Development Community (SADC)
description: The 16-member Southern African Development Community (SADC) is a regional economic bloc. It aims to promote Africa's growth by championing citizen inclusion and increased cooperation and integration of African states.

title: German election 2025
description: Friedrich Merz's center-right CDU, together with its CSU sister party, won Germany's 2025 parliamentary election. The far-right populist Alternative for Germany saw massive support across the east, coming in second.

title: Robert Koch Institute (RKI)
description: The Robert Koch Institute (RKI) is Germany's public health institute. During the COVID-19 outbreak its responsibility for federal disease control and prevention made it a pivotal agency.

title: Disability
description: Around 15% of the world's population, or estimated 1 billion people, live with disabilities. International Day of Persons with Disabilities is marked every year on Dec 3 to raise awareness and understanding.

title: Hayat Tahrir al-Sham (HTS)
description: HTS is one of the most influential rebel groups in Syria. Its offensive in December 2024 led to the ousting of longtime President Bashar Assad.

title: Pelicot trial
description: After years of horrific abuse, Gisele Pelicot emerged as a feminist hero. She stood up to abusers with dignity and forced society to examine views on sexual violence, rape and, as she said, made "shame switch sides."

title: Trinidad and Tobago
description: Trinidad and Tobago is the Caribbean's southernmost island country, off the coast of Venezuela. Home to around 1.4 million people, it's made up two main and many smaller islands. The capital is Port of Spain, Trinidad.

title: Infectious diseases
description: In humans, infectious diseases are disorders that are caused by, in most cases, microscopic organisms and material, such as bacteria, viruses, fungi and spores, and parasites.

title: Photography
description: Photography is the practice of creating images by recording light. It is an important tool for documentation and journalism, but also an influential medium for fine art.

title: Colonialism
description: Colonialism is the practice of one power dominating another area, country or people. It can be political, economic, social or cultural in nature. It is often achieved through violence and exploitation.

title: Aleksandar Vucic
description: Aleksandar Vucic is a Serbian politician and founding member of the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS). He was prime minister from 2014 to 2017 and has been president since April 2017.

title: Trump tariffs
description: Donald Trump's "America First" policies include measures aimed at reducing trade deficits and boosting domestic manufacturing. While supporters argue they protect US jobs, critics warn of massive disruption.

title: East African Community (EAC)
description: The East African Community (EAC) aims to improve the lives of the people living in its eight partner states (Burundi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Rwanda, Somalia, South Sudan, Tanzania and Uganda).

title: Javier Milei
description: Javier Gerardo Milei is an Argentine right-wing libertarian politician and economist who has served as president of Argentina since 2023.

title: Catholic Church
description: The Roman Catholic Church is the largest church within Christianity.

title: Western Balkans
description: The Western Balkans is a political term used for six countries in southeastern Europe: Albania, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia. None of these countries are members of the EU.

title: Albin Kurti
description: Albin Kurti is prime minister of Kosovo and leader of the leftist Vetevendosje, the largest political party in Kosovo.

title: Kyriakos Mitsotakis
description: Kyriakos Mitsotakis is a Greek politician. He has been the leader of the conservative New Democracy party since 2016 and prime minister of Greece since 2019.

title: Economic Community of Central African States (ECCAS)
description: ECCAS comprises 11 member states: Angola, Burundi, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Congo, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Rwanda and Sao Tome and Principe.

title: US-Europe relations
description: The Trump administration's "America First" national security strategy marks a seismic shift in historic ties between the United States and Europe.

title: Revealing what's hidden: DW Investigations
description: At DW's investigative unit, journalists are bringing to light what others are trying to hide. Often for months we try to find evidence for wrongdoings, go through extensive data or try to find hidden sources.

title: World Trade Organization (WTO)
description: The World Trade Organization (WTO) is the global body that regulates international trade, ensuring fair rules and resolving disputes to facilitate smooth trade between member states.

title: Rudolf Steiner
description: Rudolf Steiner was an Austro-Croatian spiritual thinker who founded the anthroposophy movement in the early 20th century. He is best known today for Waldorf schools, Weleda cosmetics and biodynamic farming.

title: Friedrich Nietzsche
description: Friedrich Nietzsche (1844-1900) was a German philosopher and author who today is considered one of the most important modern thinkers. His best-known ideas include "God is dead," nihilism and the "Übermensch."

title: Red Army Faction (RAF)
description: The Red Army Faction was a West German far-left militant group founded in the 1970s. It conducted murders of politicians and Business Leaders and bank robberies.

title: Defense and military spending
description: Defense policies are changing rapidly, and military spending is surging worldwide amid growing conflicts and tensions.

title: African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA)
description: The AGOA trade agreement granted eligible sub-Saharan African countries duty-free access to the US market. It expired in September 2025 after the Trump administration chose not to renew it.

title: African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA)
description: The AfCFTA, an African Union free trade project, is the world's largest free trade area, both in terms of its geographical scope and the number of participating countries.

title: African Development Bank (AfDB)
description: The African Development Bank (AfDB), established in 1964, is a multilateral development finance institution headquartered in Abidjan, Ivory Coast. It finances African governments with the aim of industrializing Africa.

title: Lars Klingbeil
description: Vice-Chancellor, Finance Minister, co-leader of Germany's oldest party, the center-left Social Democrats (SPD): Lars Klingbeil has become one of Germany's most powerful politicians.

title: Pope Leo XIV
description: Chicago-born Robert Francis Prevost was elected as head of the Catholic Church on May 8, 2025, succeeding the late Pope Francis. He is the first pope to hold US citizenship. Pope Leo XIV is also a national of Peru.

title: Johann Wadephul
description: Johann Wadephul is a seasoned foreign policy expert with the center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU). He became Germany's foreign minister in early 2025.

title: Alexander Dobrindt
description: Alexander Dobrindt took Office as Germany's Federal Interior Minister on May 6,2025.

title: Israel-Iran 12-day war
description: In June 2025, the US and Israel launched airstrikes and bombed key Iranian nuclear facilities, including uranium enrichment sites, in a 12-day war.

title: Bärbel Bas
description: Bärbel Bas is the co-chairperson of the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) and federal labor minister.

title: Digital Services Act (DSA)
description: The European Union's Digital Services Act (DSA) requires large online platforms and search engines to protect European consumers online and more effectively police their content.

title: Robert F. Kennedy Jr.
description: Robert F. Kennedy Jr. Is the US Secretary of Health and Human Services in President Donald Trump's cabinet. He is a known vaccine skeptic and propagates debunked claims that certain vaccines cause autism in children.

title: Marco Rubio
description: Republican Marco Rubio serves as US secretary of state under President Donald Trump. He previously represented Florida in the US Senate. Rubio has hardline views on immigration and is a staunch Israel supporter.

title: MAGA (Make America Great Again) movement
description: "Make America Great Again" (MAGA) was a slogan Donald Trump first used during his 2016 US presidential campaign. Today, the term describes Americans who enthusiastically support Trump and his right-wing policies.

title: Vaccines and vaccination
description: A vaccine is a biological solution that helps people build up immunity to a particular disease. The safety and efficiency of many vaccines have been proven, but vaccine skeptism is on the rise.

title: Antigua and Barbuda
description: A twin-island Caribbean nation, Antigua and Barbuda is known for its beaches, rainforests and resorts. Tourism is the backbone of its economy, and the country has an expensive cost of living due to its limited resources.

title: St. Kitts and Nevis
description: A dual-island nation in the Caribbean, St. Kitts and Nevis is the smallest sovereign state in the Western Hemisphere. A popular tourist destination, the country has shifted away from agriculture to light manufacturing.

title: St. Vincent and the Grenadines
description: St. Vincent and the Grenadines is a Caribbean nation that once belonged to the French and British. Part of the trans-Atlantic slave trade, the majority of its people are descendants of African slaves.

title: Konrad Adenauer
description: Konrad Adenauer (5.1.1876–19.4.1967) was the first chancellor of West Germany (1949–1963). He worked to restore the economy and align West Germany firmly with Western Europe and the United States.

title: Islam in Europe
description: There are an estimated 45 million Muslims in Europe, making Islam the second largest religion there after Christianity. As a result of high immigration and birth rates, it is also the fastest growing religion in Europe.

title: Contraception
description: There is a range of contraceptive methods. Some, such as the pill and intrauterine devices (IUDs), focus on preventing pregnancy. Others, such as condoms, also protect against sexually transmitted infections (STIs).

title: Charlie Kirk
description: Charlie Kirk was a Donald Trump ally and a key political activist in the MAGA movement. He was killed by a sniper while speaking on a college campus in Utah in September 2025, reigniting the issue of political violence.

title: Gen Z and student protests
description: Youth demonstrations have grown and spread in several parts of the world, including in Nepal, Bangladesh, Kenya, Morocco, Madagascar, Paraguay and Peru. Many have protested corruption and demanded government reforms.

title: Timor-Leste
description: Formerly called East Timor, Timor-Leste became independent in 2002 following years of civil war and Indonesian occupation. It is set to become the newest member of Southeast Asia's regional ASEAN bloc.

title: Uzbekistan
description: Uzbekistan is a doubly landlocked Central Asian country and former Soviet republic. It's the most populous nation in Central Asia, home to nearly 37 million people.

title: Turkmenistan
description: Turkmenistan is one of the most reclusive and authoritarian countries in the world. A former Soviet republic, it has been ruled since 2006 by the father-and-son duo: Gurbanguly Berdymukhamedov and his son Serdar.

title: Tajikistan
description: Tajikistan is a former Soviet republic that is home to around 10 million people. President Emomali Rakhmon has ruled the poor nation, bordering China, Afghanistan and fellow ex-Soviet Central Asian nations, since 1992.

title: COP30 Brazil
description: The 2025 UN climate summit took place in Belem, in the Brazilian Amazon. Negotiators discussed climate finance, the worsening impacts of rising temperatures and the need for greater action.

title: US politics
description: "All politics is local," as the saying goes. But when it comes to the decisions made by politicians in the United States, the effects can often be felt around the world.

title: Eyes and vision
description: The eyes are our most important sensory organs for seeing. They transmit light stimuli and enable orientation in space.

title: Traditional Medicine
description: Traditional medicine comprises traditional healing methods that are still used in many cultures today.

title: Epstein files
description: The Epstein files are documents related to charges brought against convicted pedophile Jeffrey Epstein of sex trafficking girls and young women.

title: Solar system
description: The solar system is Earth's cosmic neighborhood, consisting of eight planets, five dwarf plants and thousands of smaller objects that orbit the sun.

title: Mosquitoes
description: Mosquitos are flying insects found in most parts of the world. There are more than 3,500 mosquito species. A fraction of them are vectors — they carry and spread diseases. But they are also vital for healthy ecosystems.

title: Nicolas Maduro
description: Ousted Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro is on trial in the US on drug-trafficking charges. He was elected in 2013 but subsequent votes were widely disputed. In January 2026, he was captured in an unprecedented US raid.

title: 2026 Iran protests
description: Protests sparked by Iran's ailing economy have spread across the country, with demonstrators calling for a change of government and "death to the dictator." Thousands have been killed as authorities try to crush dissent.

title: Female genital mutilation
description: FGM refers to the practice of partially or fully removing external female genitalia. The global practice is a violation of women's rights that can have "short-term or lifelong health impacts," according to the UN.

title: Women's health
description: Women's health is a general term that describes a wide range of health issues that are either specific to women, such as menstruation and pregnancy, or those that affect women differently from men, such as heart disease.

title: Menstruation
description: Menstruation is part of a mostly, monthly hormonal cycle that starts with the shedding of the lining of a woman's uterus. It is also known as the menstrual period.

title: US ICE agency
description: The US agency Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is conducting nationwide raids targeting what it considers unauthorized immigrants. It has come under fire for crackdowns such as in Minneapolis, Minnesota.

title: Shehbaz Sharif
description: Shehbaz Sharif serves as the prime minister of Pakistan, having assumed office for a second term in 2024 after previously holding the position from 2022 to 2023.

title: Bola Ahmed Tinubu
description: Bola Tinubu is Nigeria's president since 2023 serving as the leader of Africa's most populous democracy. He has pledged to address rising insecurity as well as economic challenges, including inflation and unemployment.

title: Iran war's economic impact
description: The Iran war and the disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz is making everything from energy and transport to fertilizer and food more expensive.

title: Hantavirus
description: Hantavirus spreads through contact with infected rodents or their urine, droppings or saliva. It can cause severe illness and in some cases death, and there is no approved treatment or vaccine.

title: Montenegro
description: Montenegro is a country in southeastern Europe with an estimated population of about 623,000. Its capital is Podgorica. It is one of the six Western Balkan states and an EU candidate country.

title: Citizenship and visas
description: Granting citizenship is seen as a way of binding a person to a country. In recent years, citizenship has come under pressure due to increasingly polarized politics about migration, economic ties and citizens' rights.

title: Andy Burnham
description: Andy Burnham is Britain's prime minister, the country's seventh in the decade since the notorious Brexit referendum. The former Manchester mayor is one of the UK's most popular politicians.

title: India's Cockroach movement
description: The Cockroach Janta Party is an Indian protest movement against the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party. Initially aimed at India's education minister, it has expanded to focus on unemployment and a failing education system.

title: Solar eclipse
description: When the moon passes directly between the sun and the Earth, throwing our planet into a shade of darkness for a brief moment, that's a solar eclipse.

title: Ceuta crisis
description: At the end of July, a large movement of migrants crossed the border from Morocco into Ceuta, a Spanish North African exclave. The crisis has reignited a debate about migration throughout the EU.

title: Gianni Infantino
description: Gianni Infantino has been FIFA president since 2016. He has come under intense pressure since a plan to partially privatize FIFA tournaments like the men's World Cup became public. This proposal has since been dropped.

title: Europe-Russia relations
description: Amid severe tensions with Russia over its hybrid warfare, including drone attacks and disinformation, Europe is boosting its defenses.

title: Elections in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania
description: The elections in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania on September 20 could be a make-or-break moment for Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

title: US midterm elections 2026
description: In the 2026 US midterms, Democrats hope to wrest the Congressional majority from Donald Trump's Republicans.

title: Israel to close all West Bank land crossings on election day
description: After a deadly attack which killed two Israeli soldiers on Friday, the Israeli military has said all land border points between Israel and the occupied West Bank will be closed during Tuesday's election.

title: India news: Rahul Gandhi urges protest against voter deletions, announces November 1 rally
description: India's opposition leader Rahul Gandhi has accused the ruling BJP of "vote theft" and urged people to join a rally in Delhi on November 1. The call comes amid protests over revision of electoral rolls. DW has more.

title: Top stories in 90 seconds
description: DW brings you the top international news stories in brief.

title: A fire has flared up again at Adolf Hitler's Eagle's Nest retreat in southern Germany
description: Fire broke out again overnight at a former mountain retreat used by Nazi dictator Adolf Hitler. Meanwhile, a survey shows most people in Germany feel the days of the governing coalition are numbered. DW has more.

title: 法国抗议活动持续 千余人被捕
description: 法国的示威活动持续。周六，数十万人再次走上街头。警方逮捕了1000多人。不过，与上周末相比，暴力事件有所减少。

title: В Воронеже умер националист и провоенный активист Михаил Маваши, СК выясняет причины смерти
description: В Воронеже умер Михаил Маваши - рэпер, националист и сторонник войны России против Украины. Созданное им движение "Северный человек" проводило антимигрантские акции. Следствие проверяет обстоятельства его смерти.

title: Концерт Максима Галкина в Стамбуле отменен из-за обвинений в "произраильской" позиции
description: После призывов турецких СМИ и организаций концерт Максима Галкина в Стамбуле был отменен по решению местных властей. Шоумена обвинили в поддержке действий Израиля и пригрозили проведением акции протеста в день концерта.

title: A day in the life of a Tbilisi student
description: 19-year-old student Mariam lives in Tbilisi – a city torn between tradition and transformation. She shares her vision for Georgia – and a future within the EU.

title: Living off-grid in one of London’s richest suburbs
description: Life on the steps of a luxury London home, a student’s guide to Tbilisi, and a trip to Italy's Amalfi Coast.

title: Audi kündigt Milliarden-Investition in den USA an - US-Präsident Trump zeigt sich zufrieden
description: Die Volkswagen-Tochter Audi baut ein eigenes Werk in den USA. Angekündigt wurde das auf einer Wahlkampfveranstaltung der Republikaner von US-Präsident Donald Trump. Noch sind allerdings Fragen offen.

title: Leben ohne Geld in einem der reichsten Londoner Stadtviertel
description: Wie es sich auf den Stufen einer Londoner Luxusvilla lebt, was eine Studentin an ihrer Heimatstadt Tiflis schätzt und ein Reisetipp für die Amalfiküste.

title: France: Hundreds arrested after nationwide protests
description: The French government says more than 1,000 people were arrested following nationwide protests on Saturday. Police and elite security forces were out in force across the country as clashes broke out.
author_name: Wesley Dockery, Richard Connor, Timothy Jones

title: Ein Obdach im Londoner Nobelviertel
description: In London dient eines der teuersten Häuser einem Obdachlosen als Zuhause. Anders Fernstedt hat sich dort mit Spenden einen einzigartigen Wohnraum geschaffen.

title: Bulgaria holds presidential elections amid divisions over Ukraine war
description: Bulgarians are voting in presidential elections amid security concerns over attacks on ships in the Black Sea. The vote for the largely ceremonial post is seen as a test of the popularity of Prime Minister Rumen Radev.

title: Ein Tag im Leben einer Studentin in Tiflis
description: Die 19-jährige Studentin Mariam führt uns durch ihre Heimatstadt, die von Traditionen und Brüchen geprägt ist. Sie hofft, dass Georgien einmal Teil der EU wird.

title: Вучич борется за сохранение власти на выборах в Сербии: движение студентов бросило вызов правящей партии
description: В Сербии проходят досрочные парламентские выборы, исход которых может определить политическое будущее Вучича. Его партии противостоит новое движение "Студенты побеждают", возникшее после протестов в Нови-Саде.

title: Serbia election: Can student-led opposition end Aleksandar Vucic's grip on power?
description: Nearly two years after a deadly railway station collapse sparked mass anti-corruption protests, Serbians are voting in a closely fought election that could end Aleksandar Vucic's grip on power.

title: Of old and new Nazis
description: In 1961, Hannah Arendt attended the trial of Adolf Eichmann, Nazi bureaucrat of the Holocaust and saw in him the “banality of evil.” And a new novel asks how right-wing hatred arises. Stories of guilt and silence.

title: Starlink disruption exposes Ukraine's dependence on satellites
description: After last week's Starlink and Starshield disruption, Ukraine says vital satellite communications are fully restored. But the incident raised questions about Kyiv's military dependence on the technology.

title: How a centrist candidate with Moroccan roots hopes to oust right-wing Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu
description: As Israel prepares to vote, Gadi Eisenkot is leveraging his Moroccan heritage in Likud strongholds such as Sderot. From historical divides to October 7, identity and trauma are redefining the city's political loyalties.

title: В Барселоне после ночных беспорядков задержали 128 человек, большинство - несовершеннолетние
description: После несанкционированной акции в центре Барселоны полиция задержала 128 человек, включая 73 несовершеннолетних. Во время беспорядков и нападений на магазины пострадали 15 сотрудников полиции.

title: Kehlsteinhaus am Obersalzberg abgebrannt: Psychisch kranker Verdächtiger festgenommen
description: Der Brand an Hitlers Kehlsteinhaus im früheren Nazi-Sperrgebiet Obersalzberg war gelöscht. Nun musste die Feuerwehr in der Nacht erneut ausrücken.

title: Российские войска ночью и утром атаковали Украину: не менее пяти погибших, более 20 человек ранены
description: При ночных российских ударах по Днепропетровской области погибли четыре человека, еще 13 получили ранения, среди них - 11-летняя девочка. В Харькове один погибший, в Виннице шестеро ранены при ударе по многоэтажке.

title: 墙外文摘：习近平为什么不敢选接班人？
description: 中共二十届五中全会即将召开，习近平为什么迟迟不选接班人？有评论指出，推迟选择可以保住他眼下的权威，却可能让政策失去有力的守护者；而册立接班人，则会赋予一名下属不断增长、他无法完全预料的权力。

title: Adolf Eichmann: Trial of a Nazi criminal
description: In May 1960, Adolf Eichmann was kidnapped in Buenos Aires by Mossad agents. He was responsible for the murder of millions of Jews. This is a story about Nazi hunters, justice, and a trial that shook the world.

title: US accuses Canada of meddling in midterm elections
description: The Canada-US trade dispute has taken a political turn, with US officials alleging "potential Canadian interference" ahead of the midterm elections. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has rejected the accusation.

title: В центре Белгорода после массированного удара дронов ВСУ погиб человек, повреждены десятки домов
description: При массированной атаке дронов на объекты в Белгороде погиб один человек, еще 14 получили ранения. Повреждены более 30 многоквартирных домов и автомобилей, сообщают местные власти.

title: Climate protection at all costs?: The green race for Africa
description: The carbon credits market is booming as Europeans invest in CO₂ offset projects in Africa. How are these projects impacting people there?

title: Klimaschutz um jeden Preis? - Der grüne Wettlauf um Afrika
description: Der Markt für Carbon Credits boomt. Europäer setzen auf Projekte zur CO₂-Kompensation in Afrika. Was bedeuten sie für die Menschen dort?

title: In Sri Lanka, wild elephants increasingly clash with humans
description: As their habitat shrinks, wild elephants are entering Sri Lankan villages in search of food. More than a hundred people, and many more animals, die in these unpredictable encounters every year.

title: Uta Thofern
description: Als die Berliner Mauer fiel, war Uta Thofern gerade mal drei Tage bei ihrem ersten Radiojob in Luxemburg. Seitdem haben sie die Weltnachrichten nicht mehr losgelassen...

title: Marcel Fürstenau
description: Politik ist viel mehr als Regierung und Opposition, findet Marcel Fürstenau. Deshalb reizen ihn Menschen, die gerne Geschichten erzählen oder etwas verheimlichen wollen.

title: Joscha Weber
description: Als Head of Fact-checking spürt Joscha Weber mit seinem Team Desinformation, Fake News, Manipulation und Propaganda auf - und setzt ihnen Fakten entgegen.

title: Bernd Riegert
description: Deutschland und Europa sind Bernds Leidenschaft. Welche Rolle spielt Deutschland in der EU? Warum funktioniert die EU? Was haben die Menschen von diesem einmaligen Experiment?

title: Henrik Böhme
description: Wirtschaft ist Henriks Leidenschaft. Was womit zusammenhängt, wem was gehört. Wer das Sagen hat. Und wer wirklich was zu sagen hat.

title: Peter Hille
description: Peter Hille befasst sich mit Entwicklungshilfepolitik, Medienentwicklungen und macht Reportagen zu Themen aus Politik und Gesellschaft in Deutschland.

title: Christian F. Trippe
description: Was wurde aus den Menschen und den Ländern Osteuropas, die früher zum sowjetischen Machtbereich gehörten? Diese Frage treibt Christian Trippe um.

title: Volker Wagener
description: Volker Wagener beschäftigt sich überwiegend mit Südosteuropa, insbesondere mit Blick auf die Westbalkan-Länder. Immer wieder schreibt er auch Beiträge zu gesellschaftlichen und historischen Themen.

title: Stefan Nestler
description: Stefan Nestler arbeitet seit mehr als 30 Jahren für die DW, seit über 25 Jahren in der Sportredaktion. Seine journalistische Neugier hat er nicht verloren.

title: Jens Thurau
description: Jens Thurau berichtet über Innen- und Klimapolitik. Dabei legt er einen Schwerpunkt auf die Grünen und ihre Entwicklung zu einer der stärksten politischen Kräfte in Deutschland.

title: Christoph Hasselbach
description: Wie verschiebt sich die geopolitische Macht? Welche Bündnisse haben Bestand, und welche neuen entstehen? Behält Europa seinen Platz in der Welt? Das sind die Fragen, die Christoph zu beantworten versucht.

title: Alexander Freund
description: Ob Archäologie, Naturwissenschaften, Tierwelt oder Medizin - Wissenschaft ist faszinierend. Alexander Freund versucht, wegweisende Entwicklungen aus der Wissenschaft möglichst interessant und verständlich zu erklären.

title: Thomas Mösch
description: Thomas beobachtet seit vier Jahrzehnten die Entwicklungen in Subsahara-Afrika. Besonders gut kennt er sich in Westafrika aus.

title: Bartosz Dudek
description: Sein Spezialgebiet ist das polnisch-deutsche Verhältnis.

title: Kersten Knipp
description: Kersten Knipp verfolgt die politische Entwicklung in Nahost und Nordafrika. Zudem beobachtet er die romanischen Länder in Europa und Lateinamerika.

title: Rodion Ebbighausen
description: Südostasiens Diversität in politischer, wirtschaftlicher und kultureller Hinsicht faszinieren Rodion Ebbighausen seit fast 20 Jahren.

title: Martin Muno
description: Wie wird aus Ideen soziale Realität? Und wie können wir im digitalen Zeitalter Wirklichkeit und Wahn auseinanderhalten? Das sind Fragen, die Martin Muno interessieren.

title: Claus Stäcker
description: Seit der Studenten- und Jungreporterzeit im südafrikanischen Wendejahr 1994 blieb das Herz am Kap der Guten Hoffnung und die Hoffnung für Afrika der Antrieb für alle journalistische Berichterstattung

title: Alexander Andreev
description: Alexander Andreev schreibt seit 1990 für die DW und kommentiert regelmäßig aktuelle politische und gesellschaftliche Ereignisse in Bulgarien und Europa. Von 2008 bis 2022 leitete er die bulgarische DW-Redaktion.

title: Astrid Prange de Oliveira
description: Menschenrechte, Migration, Mission: Ihre Arbeit als Brasilienkorrespondentin hat den Blick von Astrid Prange de Oliveira auf ihre Heimat Deutschland und globale Herausforderungen verändert.

title: Konstantin Eggert
description: Er ist Journalist und Kolumnist, führt Interviews mit bekannten Politikern, Intellektuellen und Kulturschaffenden, er spricht mit denen, über die gesprochen wird und deren Meinung man hören will.

title: Spiros Moskovou
description: Spiros Moskovou wurde 1960 in Athen geboren und zog 1983 nach Köln. Er studierte in diesen beiden Städten und arbeitete anschließend als Journalist. 1985 kam er zur griechischen Redaktion der DW.

title: Matthias von Hein
description: Entdecker, Erzähler, Erklärer. Matthias treibt die Leidenschaft für die Nachricht hinter der Nachricht, für Zusammenhänge, für Hintergründe.

title: Sabine Kinkartz
description: Wie funktioniert Deutschland und wie geht es den Menschen in diesem Land? Das immer wieder neu zu ergründen, treibt Sabine Kinkartz an. Sie sucht weniger die Schlagzeile als vielmehr die Geschichte dahinter.

title: Andreas Sten-Ziemons
description: Andreas Sten-Ziemons - halber Arzt und ganzer Sportwissenschaftler - ist seit 2006 bei der DW und arbeitet seit 2008 für die Sportredaktion.

title: Dragoslav Dedovic
description: Seit 2018 schreibt Dragoslav Dedović die Kolumne "Aufzeichnungen von der Mündung" für die serbische Website der DW, die sich zu einer beliebten Lektüre bei DW-Medienpartnern in Serbien und Montenegro entwickelt hat.

title: Fabian Schmidt
description: Überraschendes und Ungewohntes ist Fabian Schmidts Leidenschaft. Und davon gibt es in Wissenschaft, Forschung und Entwicklung mehr als genug - von den kleinsten Nano-Welten bis in die Unendlichkeit des Universums.

title: Thomas Klein
description: Thomas Klein arbeitet seit 2008 als freier Journalist und Videograph in der Sportredaktion der DW. Er ist als Reporter unterwegs und berichtet als Autor für Online, TV und Social Media.

title: Zoran Arbutina
description: Geboren 1961 in Zagreb, Kroatien, damals Teil Jugoslawiens. Studium der Philosophie und der Vergleichenden Literaturwissenschaft, journalistisch tätig seit der Mitte der 1980er Jahre.

title: Andrey Gurkov
description: Andrey Gurkov ist Experte auf dem Gebiet der europäischen Märkte, für Wirtschaft und Finanzen.

title: Manuela Kasper-Claridge
description: Nutzerorientiert, vertrauenswürdig und vielfältig - das sind Manuela Kasper-Claridges Leitlinien für den Journalismus der DW.

title: Sandra Petersmann
description: Tiefe Recherchen und Afghanistan haben einen besonderen Platz in Sandras Leben, seit sie 1993 als junge Radio-Reporterin ihre ersten Geschichten aus Kabul produzierte.

title: Egon Ramms
description: Bis zu seiner Pensionierung 2010 war Egon Ramms Vorgesetzter der ISAF-Befehlshaber

title: Frank Hofmann
description: Frank Hofmann, Senior Correspondent mit den Schwerpunkten Europa, Sicherheit und internationale Beziehungen. Er hat als Korrespondent in Brüssel, Paris, Sarajewo, Zagreb und als Studioleiter in Kiew gearbeitet.

title: Mathias Bölinger
description: Mathias Bölinger hat viele Jahre über Ostasien und Osteuropa berichtet. Als China-Korrespondent erlebte er den Beginn der Proteste in Hongkong und in der Ukraine den Kriegsausbruch. Leitet das Investigativteam der DW.

title: Nina Werkhäuser
description: Nina Werkhäuser recherchiert und schreibt über Sicherheitspolitik, geopolitische Fragen und globale Konflikte.

title: Debarati Guha
description: Für Debarati ist das Persönliche politisch. Sie erzählt gerne Geschichten über das Leben und seine Herausforderungen. Erfahrungen wurzeln für sie in der politischen Situation und der Ungleichheit der Geschlechter.

title: Jens Krepela
description: Jens Krepela arbeitet seit seinem Volontariat 2003 für die Deutsche Welle. Er war Reporter und News-Anchor im Fernsehen und berichtet inzwischen als freier Journalist für alle Ausspielwege der DW.

title: Olivia Gerstenberger
description: Olivia Gerstenberger arbeitet seit 2008 als freie Journalistin in der Sportredaktion der Deutschen Welle, zunächst als Moderatorin und Autorin, später auch im Online-Journalismus.

title: Ines Pohl
description: Als Büroleiterin verantwortlich für die Berichterstattung aus den USA. Im Mittelpunkt stehen dabei immer die Menschen und die Frage, was dieses Land noch zusammen hält.

title: Shamil Shams
description: Shamil Shams schreibt ausführlich über den politischen Islam, die Konflikte in Afghanistan und Pakistan sowie ganz allgemein über Politik und Gesellschaft in Südasien.

title: Andreas Becker
description: Andreas moderiert außerdem den wöchentlichen Podcast "Wirtschaft im Gespräch" und ist einer der Macher der investigativen Podcast-Reihe "Cannabis Cowboys".

title: Jan D. Walter
description: Jan kam als Lateinamerika-Experte zur DW. Inzwischen steht er in Diensten der deutschen Zentralredaktion, um unseren User*innen verständliche Informationen zu geben, die ihnen valide Argumente für Diskussionen liefern.

title: Rosalia Romaniec
description: Politik ist ihre Leidenschaft. Mit den Schwerpunkten Außen- und Sicherheitspolitik sowie Nachrichtendienste begleitet Rosalia Romaniec seit Jahren äußerst relevante Themen.
